sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马斯。

sentences.en: Hey, Roman.
sentences.zh: 嘿，罗曼。

sentences.en: Hey, Delaney Hall.
sentences.zh: 嘿，德莱尼·霍尔。

sentences.en: You're the executive producer of this here show.
sentences.zh: 你是这个节目的执行制片人。

sentences.en: Yes, I am.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是。

sentences.en: And I'm going to be telling our story this week.
sentences.zh: 本周将由我来讲述我们的故事。

sentences.en: I want to start back in November 2016.
sentences.zh: 我想从2016年11月说起。

sentences.en: It was election night.
sentences.zh: 那是选举之夜。

sentences.en: Who could forget?
sentences.zh: 谁能忘得了呢？

sentences.en: And somewhere in New York City, there was a group of friends watching the results come in.
sentences.zh: 在纽约市的某个地方，有一群朋友正在观看计票结果。

sentences.en: A few of them had been low-level volunteers for the Hillary Clinton campaign.
sentences.zh: 他们中几个人曾是希拉里·克林顿竞选团队的基层志愿者。

sentences.en: Donald Trump has won the state of Florida.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普赢得了佛罗里达州。

sentences.en: Donald Trump will win Ohio.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普将赢得俄亥俄州。

sentences.en: Donald Trump will carry the state of Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普将拿下威斯康星州。

sentences.en: He will win Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 他将赢得威斯康星州。

sentences.en: And the results were not what they were expecting.
sentences.zh: 结果并非他们所预期的那样。

sentences.en: And the wall comes tumbling down.
sentences.zh: 那道“蓝墙”轰然倒塌。

sentences.en: This is the blue wall that Hillary Clinton had talked about.
sentences.zh: 这就是希拉里·克林顿曾谈到的“蓝墙”。

sentences.en: And as they watched, they were getting more and more upset.
sentences.zh: 随着计票的进行，他们变得越来越沮丧。

sentences.en: The mood was very bad at that point.
sentences.zh: 当时的气氛非常糟糕。

sentences.en: We still didn't believe it was real.
sentences.zh: 我们仍然不敢相信这是真的。

sentences.en: We wondered if there was a counting error or if it was all a big cosmic joke.
sentences.zh: 我们怀疑是不是计票出了错，或者这一切只是个巨大的宇宙玩笑。

sentences.en: Um, so yeah, shock bordering on depression, basically.
sentences.zh: 嗯，没错，基本上是处于一种濒临抑郁的震惊状态。

sentences.en: Okay, so who is that and what's up with his voice?
sentences.zh: 好吧，那个人是谁？他的声音怎么回事？

sentences.en: So that is a member of the group that was there that night.
sentences.zh: 那是那天晚上在场的一位成员。

sentences.en: And we have agreed to keep him anonymous, which is why his voice sounds like that.
sentences.zh: 我们同意对他保密，这就是为什么他的声音听起来那样。

sentences.en: Um, I'll explain more later.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我稍后再解释。

sentences.en: Okay, it's very mysterious.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这太神秘了。

sentences.en: Keep going.
sentences.zh: 继续说。

sentences.en: So this group is freaking out.
sentences.zh: 所以这群人当时都快崩溃了。

sentences.en: Everybody's spiraling.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在失控。

sentences.en: There's a lot of existential dread going on.
sentences.zh: 那种存在主义的恐惧感非常强烈。

sentences.en: Like, what is this going to mean?
sentences.zh: 就像是，这到底意味着什么？

sentences.en: One of my first thoughts, oddly enough, I don't even know why, I thought this is,
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，我最初的想法之一，我甚至不知道为什么，我当时想的是，

sentences.en: this guy's going to get a library.
sentences.zh: 这家伙会拥有一座图书馆。

sentences.en: Like, how do you get Donald Trump a presidential library?
sentences.zh: 比如，你要怎么给唐纳德·特朗普建一座总统图书馆？

sentences.en: In this moment, he's thinking about Donald Trump's future presidential library.
sentences.zh: 在那一刻，他想的是唐纳德·特朗普未来的总统图书馆。

sentences.en: I have to say that that was not where my head was at election night.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，那晚我可没往那方面想。

sentences.en: Nor mine.
sentences.zh: 我也没想过。

sentences.en: Nor mine.
sentences.zh: 我也没想过。

sentences.en: But this guy is actually an architect.
sentences.zh: 但这家伙其实是一位建筑师。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，原来如此。

sentences.en: And I won't say much more than that, but he does live in New York, where Trump made his career as a developer.
sentences.zh: 我不能透露更多，但他确实住在纽约，特朗普就是在那里以开发商身份起家的。

sentences.en: And so that's where this guy's head went.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是那家伙当时的想法。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, bookish isn't the first adjective when I think about Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，提到唐纳德·特朗普，“书卷气”可不是我脑海中蹦出的第一个形容词。

sentences.en: When he talks about his favorite book, he usually mentions his own ghostwritten autobiography.
sentences.zh: 当他谈到自己最喜欢的书时，通常提到的都是他那本由代笔者写的自传。

sentences.en: Yeah, he is by many accounts not a big reader.
sentences.zh: 是的，据许多人说，他并不是个爱读书的人。

sentences.en: So it seems a little contradictory at first, the idea of a Trump library.
sentences.zh: 所以，特朗普图书馆这个概念起初听起来有点矛盾。

sentences.en: But I will admit that, like this architect, I've become a little bit fascinated by the question of this hypothetical library.
sentences.zh: 但我承认，像这位建筑师一样，我也对这个假设性的图书馆问题产生了一点兴趣。

sentences.en: Where will it be?
sentences.zh: 它会建在哪里？

sentences.en: You know, what will it look like?
sentences.zh: 你知道，它会是什么样子？

sentences.en: Will it be gold?
sentences.zh: 会是金色的吗？

sentences.en: Will there be a gold-plated roller coaster?
sentences.zh: 会有镀金的过山车吗？

sentences.en: That's what I want to know.
sentences.zh: 那才是我真正想知道的。

sentences.en: But as I started learning about the history of presidential libraries more generally, I've kind of think there's actually something quite Trumpian about them.
sentences.zh: 但当我开始更广泛地了解总统图书馆的历史时，我发现它们其实有一种相当“特朗普式”的特质。

sentences.en: Like all of them, regardless of the president involved.
sentences.zh: 就像所有的总统图书馆一样，无论涉及的是哪位总统。

sentences.en: Oh, interesting.
sentences.zh: 哦，有意思。

sentences.en: Yeah, I can kind of see that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我多少能理解这一点。

sentences.en: Like they've always felt more like a museum to one person's greatness than anything else.
sentences.zh: 它们给人的感觉总是更像是一个展示个人伟大的博物馆，而非其他。

sentences.en: And that seems quite Trumpian in some ways.
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上看，这确实很“特朗普”。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是这样。

sentences.en: They're this weird mix of a historical repository of records and things that have a lot of meaning.
sentences.zh: 它们是一种奇怪的混合体，既是具有重大意义的档案记录库，

sentences.en: And they're also then this edifice, this self-congratulatory, almost fictional account of someone's achievements where all the blemishes are hidden.
sentences.zh: 同时也是一座自吹自擂、近乎虚构的成就纪念碑，掩盖了所有的瑕疵。

sentences.en: So we'll get back to this architect in a little bit.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后再回到这位建筑师的话题。

sentences.en: But first, I want to tell you about how presidential libraries came to be.
sentences.zh: 但首先，我想告诉你们总统图书馆是如何产生的。

sentences.en: Because they have always been a weird contradiction.
sentences.zh: 因为它们一直以来都是一种奇怪的矛盾体。

sentences.en: Oh, I'm excited.
sentences.zh: 哦，我好兴奋。

sentences.en: Let's do it.
sentences.zh: 开始吧。

sentences.en: So before the invention of presidential libraries, there was just chaos when it came to presidential records.
sentences.zh: 在总统图书馆发明之前，总统记录的管理简直是一团糟。

sentences.en: A lot of George Washington's papers were eaten by rats.
sentences.zh: 乔治·华盛顿的许多文件都被老鼠吃掉了。

sentences.en: A lot of other people's papers burned in fires.
sentences.zh: 其他许多人的文件则在火灾中烧毁了。

sentences.en: This is Jill Lepore.
sentences.zh: 这位是吉尔·莱波尔。

sentences.en: She's a historian at Harvard and a writer at The New Yorker.
sentences.zh: 她是哈佛大学的历史学家，《纽约客》的撰稿人。

sentences.en: And she's the host of a great podcast called The Last Archive.
sentences.zh: 她还是一个很棒的播客节目《最后的档案》的主持人。

sentences.en: And she says that in the early years of the country, people were just burning presidential papers in trash cans or pulling out all the unflattering documents and destroying them.
sentences.zh: 她说，在这个国家早期，人们只是把总统文件扔进垃圾桶烧掉，或者挑出所有不光彩的文件销毁。

sentences.en: The papers that remain give you a very distorted portrait of the person, right?
sentences.zh: 留存下来的文件会让你对那个人产生非常扭曲的印象，对吧？

sentences.en: So any evidence of scandal or corruption will have been very carefully excised by your children or your grandchildren or your wife or your widow.
sentences.zh: 所以任何关于丑闻或腐败的证据，都会被你的子女、孙辈、妻子或遗孀小心翼翼地剔除掉。

sentences.en: And for a long time, that was the state of things presidential papers were considered the private property of the president.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间里，情况就是这样，总统文件被视为总统的私有财产。

sentences.en: And what happened to them was very haphazard.
sentences.zh: 而它们的下场也非常随意。

sentences.en: It sounds like what got saved was shaped by a mix of chaos and self-intereSt.
sentences.zh: 听起来，能保存下来的东西是由混乱和私心共同决定的。

sentences.en: So on the one hand, what's left behind is kind of accidental.
sentences.zh: 一方面，留存下来的东西带有某种偶然性。

sentences.en: And on the other hand, what's left behind is the stuff that makes the person look good.
sentences.zh: 而另一方面，留存下来的都是那些能让当事人看起来光鲜亮丽的东西。

sentences.en: And it really wasn't until the progressive era, like the late 1800s, early 1900s, that that started to change in any kind of systematic way.
sentences.zh: 直到进步时代，也就是19世纪末20世纪初，这种情况才开始以某种系统性的方式发生改变。

sentences.en: And that was the era when people were starting to talk about good government and the ideas of openness and transparency.
sentences.zh: 那个时代，人们开始谈论廉洁政府以及开放和透明的理念。

sentences.en: And increasingly by the 1930s, that's understood in opposition to the secrecy of authoritarian regimes that are toppling democracies the world over, right?
sentences.zh: 到了20世纪30年代，这种理念日益被理解为与当时席卷全球、推翻民主制度的威权政权的秘密主义相对立，对吧？

sentences.en: Especially thinking of, you know, Mussolini and Hitler.
sentences.zh: 尤其是想到墨索里尼和希特勒。

sentences.en: So this is the era when the National Archives were established, you know, to care and preserve for the records of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以，正是在那个时代，国家档案馆成立了，旨在保管和保护美国政府的记录。

sentences.en: government.
sentences.zh: 在那之前，像总统文件这样的文档，只是被随意堆放在华盛顿特区各处废弃建筑的地下室和阁楼里。

sentences.en: And those documents, like presidential papers, had just been kept in basements and attics and various abandoned buildings scattered across Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这种混乱程度让我感到震惊。

sentences.en: And again, the disarray is just shocking to me.
sentences.zh: 这就像是我处理个人重要文件的方式，但这可是国家的文件啊？

sentences.en: Like, this is what I would do with my important documents, but like the documents of the nation?
sentences.zh: 总之，后来富兰克林·德拉诺·罗斯福出现了。
zh_words: 富兰克林·德拉诺·罗斯福

sentences.en: Anyway, then Franklin Delano Roosevelt came along.
sentences.zh: 在他第二个任期结束时，他已经为自己的文件制定了一个计划。

sentences.en: And by the end of his second term, he'd come up with a plan for his own papers.
sentences.zh: 他决定将他所有的文件集中存放在一个地方，并向公众开放。

sentences.en: He decided that he was going to put all his papers in one place and that it would be open to the public.
sentences.zh: 罗斯福是第一个提出“我可以建一个博物馆来纪念我的一生”这个想法的人。

sentences.en: Roosevelt was the one that came up with this idea that I could have a museum that would celebrate my life.
sentences.zh: 这位是本杰明·哈夫鲍尔。

sentences.en: This is Benjamin Huffbauer.
sentences.zh: 他是一位艺术史学家，也是总统图书馆方面的专家。

sentences.en: He's an art historian and an expert on presidential libraries.
sentences.zh: “我会拥有这个档案馆，它会是一栋建筑。”

sentences.en: And I'd have this archive and it would be a building.
sentences.zh: 他本人是个业余建筑师，所以他为那个档案馆设计了自己的小楼。

sentences.en: And he was an amateur architect, so he designed his own little building for that.
sentences.zh: 它采用荷兰殖民风格设计，其实也不算太小。

sentences.en: It was designed in the Dutch colonial style, and it wasn't actually that little.
sentences.zh: 大约有4万平方英尺。

sentences.en: It was about 40,000 square feet.
sentences.zh: 罗斯福决定把它建在海德公园，也就是他出生的地方。

sentences.en: And Roosevelt decided that it would be built in Hyde Park, New York, the place where he was born.
sentences.zh: 为了筹集资金，他向支持者求助。

sentences.en: And to raise the funds for it, he turned to his supporters.
sentences.zh: 所以罗斯福总统的支持者可以寄来10美元、20美元、50美元或100美元的支票，这些钱都用于图书馆的建设。

sentences.en: So supporters of President Roosevelt could mail in a check for $10, $20, $50, $100, and that went into the funding of the library.
sentences.zh: 建筑完工后，它就被移交给了联邦政府，由国家档案馆接管，基本上由美国政府永久运营。

sentences.en: Then once the building was completed, then it was handed over to the federal government, to the National Archives, to be run forever, basically, by the U.S.
sentences.zh: “美国档案馆的这一最新成员，是在一个民有、民治、民享的政府在各地受到攻击的时刻落成的。”

sentences.en: government.
sentences.zh: 就这样，第一个总统图书馆诞生了。

sentences.en: And this latest addition to the Archives of America is dedicated at a moment when government of the people by themselves is being attacked everywhere.
sentences.zh: 它于1941年开放。

sentences.en: And so that was it, the first presidential library.
sentences.zh: 哇，这在美国历史上似乎是很近的事。

sentences.en: It opened in 1941.
sentences.zh: 那么当它在41年开放时，人们有什么反应？

sentences.en: Wow, that seems so recent in American history.
sentences.zh: 它是如何被接受的？

sentences.en: So when this thing opened in 41, how did people react to it?
sentences.zh: 哦，很多人觉得这很荒谬。

sentences.en: Like, how was it received?
sentences.zh: 人们认为他是个自大狂。

sentences.en: Oh, a lot of people thought it was ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 有人说他想建造一座“扬基金字塔”。

sentences.en: People thought he was a megalomaniac.
sentences.zh: 当时有一幅漫画，把罗斯福描绘成圣诞老人，把总统图书馆作为礼物装进自己的长筒袜里，并说道：

sentences.en: Someone said he wanted to build a Yankee pyramid.
sentences.zh: “哦，他会感到惊喜吗？”

sentences.en: There was a comic that portrayed FDR as Santa Claus, presenting a giant present in his own stocking of the presidential library, and saying,
sentences.zh: 愿上帝保佑他。

sentences.en: Oh, won't he be surprised?
sentences.zh: 吼，吼，吼。

sentences.en: Bless his heart.
sentences.zh: 看来公众对这个图书馆的本质看得相当透彻。

sentences.en: Ho, ho, ho.
sentences.zh: 就像是罗斯福为自己建造的一座纪念碑。

sentences.en: Well, it seems like the public had a pretty good take on what the library actually was.
sentences.zh: 没错，而且还是在他活着的时候。

sentences.en: Kind of like a monument that FDR built to himself.
sentences.zh: 这在当时确实是前所未有的。

sentences.en: Yeah, and while he was alive, no less.
sentences.zh: 传统上，总统纪念碑都是在他们去世很久之后才建造的。

sentences.en: Like, that was really not done at the time.
sentences.zh: 例如，华盛顿纪念碑是在19世纪80年代中期完工的，距离乔治·华盛顿去世约85年。

sentences.en: The tradition was that monuments to presidents were built long after they had died.
sentences.zh: 林肯纪念堂于1922年落成，距离亚伯拉罕·林肯去世近60年。

sentences.en: The Washington Monument, for example, was finished in the mid-1880s, about 85 years after George Washington died.
sentences.zh: 是的，通常会有很长的时间间隔，而且只有最杰出的总统才能拥有纪念碑。

sentences.en: And the Lincoln Memorial was dedicated in 1922, nearly 60 years after Abraham Lincoln's death.
sentences.zh: 而现在，我们每位总统在世时，有时甚至在任期内，就能立刻拥有纪念碑。

sentences.en: Yeah, normally there's this big gap, and only the most exceptional presidents get a monument.
sentences.zh: 但罗斯福图书馆最终为后来的总统图书馆树立了模板。

sentences.en: And here we've got monuments right away to each president as they're still living, sometimes as they're still in office.
sentences.zh: 1955年，国会通过了《总统图书馆法》，将这种由私人建造、公共管理的机构模式制度化了。

sentences.en: But the FDR library ended up setting the template for presidential libraries going forward.
sentences.zh: 下一个建成的是位于密苏里州独立城的杜鲁门图书馆。

sentences.en: In 1955, Congress passed the Presidential Libraries Act, which formalized this idea of privately built and publicly administered institutions.
sentences.zh: 它的结构和罗斯福图书馆一样。

sentences.en: The next one that went up was the Truman Library in Independence, Missouri.
sentences.zh: 它是国家档案馆的一个分支机构。

sentences.en: And it was structured like FDRs.
sentences.zh: 里面装满了，你知道，真正重要的文件。

sentences.en: So it was a branch of the National Archives.
sentences.zh: 它确实改善了研究人员的查阅条件。

sentences.en: It was full of, you know, actual important documents.
sentences.zh: 但它的博物馆基本上也是杜鲁门的个人神殿。

sentences.en: It really did improve access for researchers.
sentences.zh: 这让我产生了一个疑问：作为美国人，我们该如何讲述自己的故事？

sentences.en: But its museum was also basically a shrine to Truman.
sentences.zh: 这位是布鲁斯·舒尔曼。

sentences.en: And it raised for me the question of, you know, how do we as Americans tell our stories?
sentences.zh: 他是波士顿大学的历史学家。

sentences.en: This is Bruce Shulman.
sentences.zh: 他参观过现存的大多数总统图书馆。

sentences.en: He's a historian at Boston University.
sentences.zh: 我们如何教授历史？

sentences.en: He has visited most of the existing presidential libraries.
sentences.zh: 我们如何谈论它？

sentences.en: How do we teach history?
sentences.zh: 我想我刚才不经意间对这些问题产生了兴趣。

sentences.en: How do we speak about it?
sentences.zh: 而且，你大概能猜到杜鲁门图书馆以及其他图书馆讲述总统故事的方式。

sentences.en: So I think I just accidentally became interested in those questions.
sentences.zh: 这本质上是一个英雄故事，讲述了一个非凡的人如何在关键时刻出现，改变了国家的命运。

sentences.en: And, you know, you can probably guess the way the presidential story gets told in the Truman Library, but also others.
sentences.zh: 这触及了档案馆所做的工作与这些神殿试图做的事情之间的本质张力，

sentences.en: It's fundamentally this heroic story about how an extraordinary person comes along at a pivotal moment in American history, changing the country's destiny.
sentences.zh: 那就是创造一种主要让人感觉良好的、对美国过去以及这位特定总统在其中所扮演角色的颂扬。

sentences.en: And that that kind of gets at the essential tension between the work that's being done in the archive and what it is those shrines are trying to do,
sentences.zh: 我认为它们是前总统们虚荣心的纪念碑，而这种虚荣心是不可估量的。

sentences.en: which is to create a largely feel-good celebration of the American past and this particular president's role in it.
sentences.zh: 这就是本周的节目。

sentences.en: I think they're monuments to the vanity of ex-presidents, which is immeasurable.
sentences.zh: 《99%隐形》由罗曼·马斯制作。

sentences.en: Well, Jill Lepore always calls it like she sees it.
sentences.zh: 吉尔·莱波雷（Jill Lepore）总是直言不讳。

sentences.en: You know, and she is not wrong.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她说得没错。

sentences.en: There are so many interesting examples of how these huge presidential egos end up manifesting in their buildings.
sentences.zh: 这些总统巨大的自我意识最终在他们的建筑中体现出来，这样的例子实在太多了。

sentences.en: But I think my favorite is the Lyndon Baines Johnson Library in Austin, Texas.
sentences.zh: 但我最喜欢的是位于德克萨斯州奥斯汀的林登·贝恩斯·约翰逊图书馆。

sentences.en: It is a stunning building.
sentences.zh: 那是一座令人惊叹的建筑。

sentences.en: It's just massive.
sentences.zh: 它非常宏大。

sentences.en: Beautiful travertine marble imported from Italy covers the entire thing, which has almost no windows, except right before the top floor,
sentences.zh: 整座建筑覆盖着从意大利进口的精美洞石，几乎没有窗户，除了顶层下方，

sentences.en: which is cantilevered out and has glass beneath it.
sentences.zh: 顶层是悬挑出来的，下方有玻璃。

sentences.en: So it looks almost like it's kind of floating.
sentences.zh: 所以它看起来几乎像是漂浮着一样。

sentences.en: It looks kind of like a cross between a space-age bureaucracy and an Egyptian pylon temple.
sentences.zh: 它看起来有点像是太空时代的官僚机构和埃及塔门神庙的结合体。

sentences.en: You really have to see pictures of it to kind of believe it.
sentences.zh: 你真的得看看它的照片，才能相信它是真的。

sentences.en: And this building was starting to go up in 1967, 1968, towards the end of LBJ's time in office.
sentences.zh: 这座建筑始建于1967年、1968年，也就是约翰逊总统任期的末期。

sentences.en: And, you know, that was a very consequential time.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，那是一个非常关键的时期。

sentences.en: There was a lot going on.
sentences.zh: 当时发生了许多事情。

sentences.en: You've got, of course, more than 500,000 American troops in Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 当然，当时有超过50万美军在越南。

sentences.en: Martin Luther King Jr., of course, is tragically assassinated.
sentences.zh: 马丁·路德·金博士当然也不幸遇刺了。

sentences.en: Robert Kennedy is tragically assassinated.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·肯尼迪也不幸遇刺了。

sentences.en: But literally in the middle of all of that chaos and tragedy, on the 10th of October, 1968, LBJ placed a call from the Oval Office to Gordon Bunshaft,
sentences.zh: 但就在所有这些混乱和悲剧之中，1968年10月10日，约翰逊总统从椭圆形办公室给戈登·邦沙夫特打了一个电话，

sentences.en: who was the architect he'd chosen to design his library.
sentences.zh: 他就是约翰逊选定的图书馆设计师。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Gordon, yes, sir.
sentences.zh: 戈登，是的，先生。

sentences.en: Gordon.
sentences.zh: 戈登。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Lyndon Johnson.
sentences.zh: 林登·约翰逊。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: Lyndon, how are you?
sentences.zh: 林登，你好吗？

sentences.en: I hope I'm not interrupting your dinner, sir.
sentences.zh: 希望我没有打扰你吃晚餐，先生。

sentences.en: No, no.
sentences.zh: 没有，没有。

sentences.en: We've finished some time.
sentences.zh: 我们已经吃完一会儿了。

sentences.en: Oh, he was definitely interrupting his dinner in that call.
sentences.zh: 哦，他打那个电话时绝对是打扰了他吃晚餐。

sentences.en: I feel like without a doubt, you know, knowing LBJ, he probably was interrupting his dinner on purpose.
sentences.zh: 我觉得毫无疑问，了解约翰逊的人都知道，他很可能是故意打扰他吃晚餐的。

sentences.en: Just to show his dominance.
sentences.zh: 只是为了展示他的权威。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: And what LBJ is calling about is that he really wants the architect to find a place in his library for a replica of the Oval Office.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊打电话是为了告诉建筑师，他非常希望在图书馆里为椭圆形办公室留出一个复制品的位置。

sentences.en: LBJ had noticed that the Truman Library had one, and he is now wanting one, too.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊注意到杜鲁门图书馆有一个，现在他也想要一个。

sentences.en: But remember, the construction of this building is already underway.
sentences.zh: 但请记住，这座建筑的施工已经在进行了。

sentences.en: I'm looking at these libraries, and is there no way in the world that we could reconstitute as nearly as possible the president's office here?
sentences.zh: 我正在看这些图书馆，难道就没有办法尽可能地在这里还原总统办公室吗？

sentences.en: Well, we haven't thought of it, but it's possible.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们还没考虑过，但这是可能的。

sentences.en: And, you know, listening to this call, the architect clearly wasn't a huge fan of this idea, but the call goes on for seven minutes and 46 seconds.
sentences.zh: 而且，听这段录音，建筑师显然不太喜欢这个主意，但通话持续了7分46秒。

sentences.en: It's a classic LBJ monologue.
sentences.zh: 这是典型的约翰逊式独白。

sentences.en: I'd rather have that than anything else about the building.
sentences.zh: 比起关于建筑的其他任何事情，我更想听这个。

sentences.en: I gather that, all right, and we'll see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了，好吧，我们会看看的。

sentences.en: I'm in there now.
sentences.zh: 我现在就在里面。

sentences.en: I'm in that office tonight, and I come in at sometimes at 6.30 in the morning, and I'm here too late.
sentences.zh: 今晚我在这间办公室里，有时早上6点半就来了，我待得太晚了。

sentences.en: And I would like for them to see just where we work, and I'd like to have the exact replica as near as possible.
sentences.zh: 我希望他们能看到我们工作的地方，我希望能有一个尽可能精确的复制品。

sentences.en: But I would accept anything.
sentences.zh: 但我接受任何方案。

sentences.en: This is fascinating to me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说太迷人了。

sentences.en: I mean, this is, psychologically, I can't quite parse this.
sentences.zh: 我是说，从心理学角度来看，我无法完全解析这一点。

sentences.en: Does he imagine, you know, not being president someday and just sitting in his, you know, like, little playset of the presidency in his library?
sentences.zh: 他是否在想象，你知道，有一天不再担任总统，只是坐在他图书馆里那个小小的总统办公室模型里？

sentences.en: It's just like, it's so odd.
sentences.zh: 这真是太奇怪了。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: And it's just, there's so much president stuff he should be doing.
sentences.zh: 而且，他本该有那么多总统事务要处理。

sentences.en: And I'm sure he is doing.
sentences.zh: 我相信他确实在处理。

sentences.en: I'm sure he is doing.
sentences.zh: 我相信他确实在处理。

sentences.en: But he has the space to also be sort of micromanaging the designs of his presidential library.
sentences.zh: 但他还有空间去微观管理他总统图书馆的设计。

sentences.en: It's very fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这非常迷人。

sentences.en: So by the late 1960s, early 1970s, every president since FDR had built himself one of these sweet new libraries.
sentences.zh: 所以到了60年代末、70年代初，自富兰克林·罗斯福以来的每一位总统都为自己建造了这些漂亮的新图书馆。

sentences.en: And actually, Herbert Hoover had built one, too, retroactively.
sentences.zh: 事实上，赫伯特·胡佛也追溯性地建了一座。

sentences.en: The libraries were becoming increasingly monumental and grandiose.
sentences.zh: 这些图书馆变得越来越宏伟壮观。

sentences.en: But interestingly, at this time, the papers of the president were still considered his personal property.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，当时总统的文件仍被视为其个人财产。

sentences.en: Whoa.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: That is really strange.
sentences.zh: 那真的很奇怪。

sentences.en: So there was, like, this new custom where, you know, presidents would voluntarily put their papers in the library.
sentences.zh: 所以当时有一种新的习俗，你知道，总统会自愿把他们的文件放进图书馆。

sentences.en: And then, you know, some of that management would be passed over to the National Archives.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，部分管理工作会移交给国家档案馆。

sentences.en: But it was basically, like, the honor system.
sentences.zh: 但这基本上是靠自觉。

sentences.en: Like, they didn't have to give everything up.
sentences.zh: 就像，他们不必交出所有东西。

sentences.en: They could just pick and choose.
sentences.zh: 他们可以挑挑拣拣。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: It was the honor system.
sentences.zh: 那是靠自觉的。

sentences.en: And can you guess which president really tested that honor system?
sentences.zh: 你能猜出哪位总统真正考验了这种自觉吗？

sentences.en: Any guesses?
sentences.zh: 有什么猜测吗？

sentences.en: Oh, I think I can get it in one.
sentences.zh: 哦，我想我一下子就能猜到。

sentences.en: We're talking about Richard Milhouse Nixon here.
sentences.zh: 我们说的是理查德·米尔豪斯·尼克松。
zh_words: 理查德·米尔豪斯·尼克松

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: The Nixon era was kind of the battle royale over who gets to control the papers of the president.
sentences.zh: 尼克松时代是一场关于谁能控制总统文件的混战。

sentences.en: And, you know, Nixon had proceeded, as everyone before him had done,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，尼克松像他之前的每个人一样行事，

sentences.en: as if all the records created by his office during his presidency were his private property and he could do with them as he wished.
sentences.zh: 仿佛他在任期间办公室产生的所有记录都是他的私有财产，他可以随心所欲地处理它们。

sentences.en: He could cull them.
sentences.zh: 他可以剔除它们。

sentences.en: He could destroy them.
sentences.zh: 他可以销毁它们。

sentences.en: And Nixon did not foresee that his records would be requested and then demanded by Congress during the investigation into his administration.
sentences.zh: 尼克松没预料到，在针对他政府的调查中，国会会要求并随后强征他的记录。

sentences.en: And when that request and demand was made, you know, he resisted it.
sentences.zh: 当这种要求和强征发生时，你知道，他进行了抵制。

sentences.en: And so Congress seized President Nixon's records and subsequently made future presidential records the property of the country rather than the property of the individual president.
sentences.zh: 于是国会没收了尼克松总统的记录，并随后规定未来的总统记录属于国家，而不是属于个别总统。

sentences.en: And they did that with the Presidential Records Act, which passed in 1978.
sentences.zh: 他们通过1978年颁布的《总统记录法》做到了这一点。

sentences.en: And the PRA says that presidential records are in the public domain and the public can see them after five years, five years after the president leaves office, you know,
sentences.zh: 《总统记录法》规定总统记录属于公共领域，公众可以在总统离任五年后查看它们，你知道，

sentences.en: with the exception of classified material.
sentences.zh: 机密材料除外。

sentences.en: Well, we're finally getting to where the way I would expect things to be.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们终于达到了我所期望的状态。

sentences.en: So the law affirmed the importance of keeping presidential records safe and available to the public.
sentences.zh: 所以法律肯定了保持总统记录安全并对公众开放的重要性。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So the law did do that.
sentences.zh: 法律确实做到了这一点。

sentences.en: But the records continued to be stored in presidential libraries.
sentences.zh: 但记录仍然存储在总统图书馆中。

sentences.en: And, you know, nothing really changed about the basically self-congratulatory vibe of most of those libraries.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，大多数图书馆那种本质上自我吹捧的氛围并没有真正改变。

sentences.en: The Nixon Library is a fascinating example.
sentences.zh: 尼克松图书馆就是一个迷人的例子。

sentences.en: For many years, the Nixon Library was actually privately run by the Richard Nixon Foundation.
sentences.zh: 多年来，尼克松图书馆实际上是由理查德·尼克松基金会私下运营的。

sentences.en: It was not affiliated with the National Archive.
sentences.zh: 它不隶属于国家档案馆。

sentences.en: And it portrayed Watergate very much from Nixon's perspective.
sentences.zh: 它非常从尼克松的角度来描述水门事件。

sentences.en: You know, the event was characterized as a quote-unquote coup by Nixon's enemies.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这一事件被尼克松的敌人定性为所谓的“政变”。

sentences.en: And the exhibit suggested that the press had behaved unethically in pursuing the story of his crimes.
sentences.zh: 展览暗示新闻界在追踪他的犯罪故事时表现得不道德。

sentences.en: Whoa.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That's bold.
sentences.zh: 那很大胆。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And it wasn't until the mid-2000s that the National Archives came in and took over the museum.
sentences.zh: 直到21世纪中期，国家档案馆才介入并接管了博物馆。

sentences.en: And when they did, they insisted that a very well-respected historian come in to create a more factually accurate Watergate exhibit.
sentences.zh: 当他们接管时，他们坚持要求一位备受尊敬的历史学家进来，创建一个更符合事实的水门事件展览。

sentences.en: And you can probably imagine members of the Richard Nixon Foundation did not like that.
sentences.zh: 你大概能想象理查德·尼克松基金会的成员不喜欢那样。

sentences.en: There was one guy who called the new exhibit a hit piece.
sentences.zh: 有个人称新展览为“攻击性文章”。

sentences.en: And the historian involved with it, he was harassed.
sentences.zh: 而参与其中的历史学家受到了骚扰。

sentences.en: He eventually resigned.
sentences.zh: 他最终辞职了。

sentences.en: Whoa.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: That's intense.
sentences.zh: 那太激烈了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And it's just, you know, it's an example of how structurally it's very hard to tell a nuanced and complex story in these libraries.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这是一个例子，说明在这些图书馆里讲述一个细致入微且复杂的故事在结构上有多么困难。

sentences.en: The president gets to select the architect that they want.
sentences.zh: 总统可以挑选他们想要的建筑师。

sentences.en: They have a role often in selecting who's going to be the director of that presidential library.
sentences.zh: 他们通常在挑选谁将成为该总统图书馆馆长方面发挥作用。

sentences.en: And the president takes an active role in designing.
sentences.zh: 而且总统在设计中扮演积极角色。

sentences.en: They're basically the head curator of their museum to themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上是自己博物馆的总策展人。

sentences.en: I should say that I talked to various employees of the presidential library system, and I've asked them, why don't you insist on more historical objectivity?
sentences.zh: 我应该说，我采访过总统图书馆系统的各种员工，我问他们，为什么你们不坚持更高的历史客观性？

sentences.en: And some of these people looked at me and said, what planet are you living on?
sentences.zh: 其中一些人看着我说，你生活在哪个星球上？

sentences.en: These people have run the country.
sentences.zh: 这些人曾经治理过国家。

sentences.en: Do you think we can tell them what to do?
sentences.zh: 你以为我们能告诉他们该怎么做吗？

sentences.en: How do you think that's going to happen?
sentences.zh: 你觉得那怎么可能发生？

sentences.en: And one of the most compelling examples of this that was described to me was from the Decision Points Theater at the George W.
sentences.zh: 有人向我描述的最令人信服的例子之一来自达拉斯乔治·W·布什图书馆的“决策点剧场”。

sentences.en: Bush Library in Dallas.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到决策点剧场。

sentences.en: Welcome to the Decision Points Theater.
sentences.zh: 乔治·W·布什在担任总统期间做出了许多艰难的决定。

sentences.en: George W.
sentences.zh: 现在你将体验一下那是什么感觉。

sentences.en: Bush made many tough decisions as president.
sentences.zh: 看看你面前的场景列表。

sentences.en: Now you'll get a flavor for what that's like.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以整个决策点体验是非常互动的。

sentences.en: Take a look at the list of scenarios in front of you.
sentences.zh: 你可以从场景菜单中进行选择。

sentences.en: Okay, so the whole Decision Points experience is very interactive.
sentences.zh: 你可以决定卡特里娜飓风过后在纽奥良该怎么做。

sentences.en: You get to choose from a menu of scenarios.
sentences.zh: 你可以决定在2008年金融危机后该怎么做。

sentences.en: You can decide what to do in New Orleans after Hurricane Katrina.
sentences.zh: 你可以决定是否要入侵伊拉克。

sentences.en: You can decide what to do following the 2008 financial crisis.
sentences.zh: 你会得到一份简报、专家的政策建议，并对该怎么做进行投票。

sentences.en: You can decide if you want to invade Iraq.
sentences.zh: 专家们不会同意你的看法。

sentences.en: You'll get a briefing, your expert policy advice, and vote on what to do.
sentences.zh: 那太神奇了。

sentences.en: The experts will not agree with you.
sentences.zh: 我非常渴望听到这些反事实是如何编写的，以证明乔治·W·布什实际上做出的每一个决定都是合理的。

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I'm very eager to hear how the counterfactuals are written to justify each of the decisions that George W.
sentences.zh: 是啊，这真的很有趣，因为它是真正互动的。

sentences.en: Bush actually made.
sentences.zh: 剧场里的观众可以投票。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，不出所料，在伊拉克战争的案例中，相当多的人选择，

sentences.en: Yeah, it's really interesting because it's genuinely interactive.
sentences.zh: 不，我不想入侵伊拉克，因为我们生活在当下。

sentences.en: The audience in this theater gets to vote.
sentences.zh: 我们知道那次行动的结果。

sentences.en: And, you know, not surprisingly, in the case of the Iraq War, a fair number of people select,
sentences.zh: 但如果你选择“不”，乔治·布什总统会出现在视频中说，不，那是错误的选择。

sentences.en: no, I do not want to invade Iraq because we're living in the present moment.
sentences.zh: 你必须，你知道，基本上，我们别无选择。

sentences.en: We know how that went.
sentences.zh: 我们别无选择。

sentences.en: But if you choose no, President George Bush comes up on the video and says, no, that's the incorrect choice.
sentences.zh: 我们别无选择。

sentences.en: You must, you know, basically, we had no choice.
sentences.zh: 我们别无选择。

sentences.en: Saddam Hussein represented too big a threat, and you must invade Iraq.
sentences.zh: 萨达姆·侯赛因构成了巨大的威胁，你们必须入侵伊拉克。

sentences.en: So the president comes on to scold you about your poor decision-making skills that didn't conform to his own.
sentences.zh: 于是总统亲自出马，斥责你决策能力低下，没有与他的决策保持一致。

sentences.en: Oh, that's amazing.
sentences.zh: 哦，那真是太神奇了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And I guess it shouldn't be that surprising to anyone at this point that we don't get a more nuanced take in a museum designed in close collaboration with Bush himself.
sentences.zh: 我想，到了现在，如果我们在一个与布什本人密切合作设计的博物馆里，却没能看到更细致入微的解读，大家应该也不会感到太惊讶了。

sentences.en: But, you know, it's still problematic.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，这仍然是个问题。

sentences.en: So this is what's troubling about this, is that this is a museum run by the federal government.
sentences.zh: 所以，这正是令人困扰的地方，因为这是一个由联邦政府运营的博物馆。

sentences.en: So you think this is the National Archives.
sentences.zh: 所以你以为这是国家档案馆。

sentences.en: They're not going to feed me something that's a lie or wrong.
sentences.zh: 他们不会给我灌输谎言或错误的信息。

sentences.en: And yet, you know, from former President Bush's point of view, this is the truth.
sentences.zh: 然而，你知道，从前总统布什的角度来看，这就是真相。

sentences.en: But it's a very particular and propagandistic truth.
sentences.zh: 但这是一种非常特殊且带有宣传色彩的真相。

sentences.en: I mean, that's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这真的很有意思。

sentences.en: Like, it's almost less problematic, less official we try to make these things.
sentences.zh: 就像，我们试图让这些东西显得不那么官方、不那么有问题，反而效果更好。

sentences.en: You know, like, I would almost have no problem if the Bush family kept, you know, like a shrine to Bush.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果布什家族只是保留一个布什纪念堂，我几乎不会有任何意见。

sentences.en: But it's almost the fact that it's a government facility that's the issue.
sentences.zh: 但问题在于，这竟然是一个政府设施。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I think it is the mixing of purposes that makes these institutions so troublesome.
sentences.zh: 我认为正是这种目的的混杂，使得这些机构变得如此令人头疼。

sentences.en: You know, it's the way there's an archive that gives legitimacy to the museum, which tells the story in a way that an actual historian never would,
sentences.zh: 你知道，档案馆赋予了博物馆合法性，而博物馆讲述故事的方式，是真正的历史学家绝不会采用的，

sentences.en: sort of lacking all the nuance and complexity that's required.
sentences.zh: 它缺乏了所有必要的细微差别和复杂性。

sentences.en: So there's another element to this story, which I talked with Joe Lepore about.
sentences.zh: 所以这个故事还有另一个层面，我和乔·勒波尔谈过。

sentences.en: And it has to do with some of the unintended consequences of the Presidential Records Act, which passed right after the Watergate scandal.
sentences.zh: 这与《总统档案法》的一些意外后果有关，该法案是在水门事件后立即通过的。

sentences.en: And, of course, it was intended to create a fuller record of each presidency.
sentences.zh: 当然，它的初衷是为每一届总统任期建立更完整的记录。

sentences.en: But she says that in some ways the opposite has happened.
sentences.zh: 但她说，在某些方面，结果恰恰相反。

sentences.en: Where people say, yeah, well, I would have put it down in a note, but then that would have been subject to the Presidential Records Act.
sentences.zh: 人们会说，是啊，我本来会把它写在便条里，但那样就会受到《总统档案法》的约束。

sentences.en: So, you know, I just called the guy.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我干脆直接给那个人打了电话。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: So it's like in that sense, it's easy to evade.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，这很容易规避。

sentences.en: From historians' vantage, these people all used to keep diaries.
sentences.zh: 从历史学家的角度来看，这些人过去都习惯写日记。

sentences.en: They're also self-important.
sentences.zh: 他们也很自负。

sentences.en: Keep endless diaries.
sentences.zh: 写个没完没了的日记。

sentences.en: And now they don't keep diaries.
sentences.zh: 而现在他们不写日记了。

sentences.en: So you don't even know who they were meeting with on a given day because they didn't want to have that written down.
sentences.zh: 所以你甚至不知道他们在某一天见了谁，因为他们不想把这些写下来。

sentences.en: Like, people have ways of avoiding creating a record.
sentences.zh: 就像，人们总有办法避免留下记录。

sentences.en: Yeah, because once you have a record, then some independent counsel can, you know, like, impeach you using those records or lawyers could dig through them.
sentences.zh: 是啊，因为一旦有了记录，某些独立检察官就可以利用这些记录弹劾你，或者律师可以翻查它们。

sentences.en: I mean, I could totally see a president just deciding, no, I don't want to deal with that.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我完全能想象一位总统直接决定：不，我不想处理那种麻烦。

sentences.en: So did these historians that you talked to have a take on what they thought the future Presidential Records would be like and how they would affect Presidential Libraries?
sentences.zh: 那么你采访的那些历史学家对未来的总统档案会有什么看法？他们认为这会如何影响总统图书馆？

sentences.en: We did talk about that.
sentences.zh: 我们确实讨论过这个问题。

sentences.en: And as the power of the presidency has grown over the course of the 20th century, the size of these institutions has grown as well.
sentences.zh: 随着总统权力的增长，在整个20世纪，这些机构的规模也随之扩大。

sentences.en: So that first library that was designed by Roosevelt cost about $7 million in today's money.
sentences.zh: 罗斯福设计的第一个图书馆在今天的货币价值中大约花费了700万美元。

sentences.en: The latest figures for the construction of the Obama Presidential Center are about $700 million.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马总统中心最新的建设预算约为7亿美元。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: It's a huge amount of money.
sentences.zh: 这是一笔巨款。

sentences.en: And then at the same time presidential power has grown, public trust in the presidency has been falling.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，随着总统权力的增长，公众对总统职位的信任度却在下降。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, I think there's some public discontent with the idea of the monumentality of these places.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你知道，我认为公众对这些地方的纪念碑性质存在一些不满。

sentences.en: I don't think the presidency has the public trust that it had when FDR proposed to Presidential Libraries.
sentences.zh: 我不认为总统职位还拥有罗斯福提议建立总统图书馆时那样的公众信任。

sentences.en: I think the presidency has betrayed the public truSt.
sentences.zh: 我认为总统职位已经辜负了公众的信任。

sentences.en: And so Jill Lepore and I think a lot of other professional historians just kind of wish the Presidential Libraries would go away.
sentences.zh: 所以吉尔·勒波尔和我，我想还有许多其他专业历史学家，都希望总统图书馆能消失。

sentences.en: Like, it's not that their archives aren't important.
sentences.zh: 并不是说它们的档案不重要。

sentences.en: They truly are.
sentences.zh: 它们确实非常重要。

sentences.en: There's no particular reason those collections couldn't be housed in one central place in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 没有特别的理由说明这些藏品不能存放在华盛顿特区的一个中心地点。

sentences.en: Yeah, that certainly makes more sense to me than having them sort of spread out around the country in different shrines to different men.
sentences.zh: 是啊，这对我来说肯定比把它们分散在全国各地，作为不同男人的不同神龛要合理得多。

sentences.en: Yeah, it makes sense to me, too.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我也觉得这很有道理。

sentences.en: And interestingly, things might actually be starting to move in that direction.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，事情可能真的开始朝着那个方向发展了。

sentences.en: So the Obama Presidential Center, for example, which we were just talking about, it is not going to hold Obama's actual presidential records.
sentences.zh: 比如我们刚才谈到的奥巴马总统中心，它将不会保存奥巴马实际的总统档案。

sentences.en: Those will be held by the National Archives in various facilities.
sentences.zh: 那些档案将由国家档案馆在各个设施中保存。

sentences.en: The center in Chicago will be the site of the museum.
sentences.zh: 芝加哥的中心将作为博物馆所在地。

sentences.en: And it will also serve other purposes as a community center, as a place for the Obama's philanthropic and diplomatic work.
sentences.zh: 它还将作为社区中心，以及奥巴马夫妇进行慈善和外交工作的场所，发挥其他作用。

sentences.en: And part of that is because it's just become really expensive for libraries to be affiliated with the National Archives.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是图书馆隶属于国家档案馆的成本已经变得非常昂贵。

sentences.en: Over the years, Congress has passed legislation requiring ex-presidents to raise massive endowments that will cover the cost of repairing and maintaining these buildings.
sentences.zh: 多年来，国会通过了立法，要求前总统筹集巨额捐赠基金，以支付修复和维护这些建筑的费用。

sentences.en: So with Trump, there are people who think that if he does manage to build a presidential library, that it might be along the lines of the Obama Center.
sentences.zh: 所以对于特朗普，有人认为如果他真的设法建造了一个总统图书馆，它可能会像奥巴马中心那样。

sentences.en: So he might build a shrine to himself, but people speculate he won't bother with the actual papers.
sentences.zh: 所以他可能会为自己建造一个神龛，但人们推测他不会费心去处理那些实际的文件。

sentences.en: Those will stay with the National Archives.
sentences.zh: 那些文件将留在国家档案馆。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: So the two purposes that have mixed in such uncomfortable ways through the history of presidential libraries, maybe, you know, they're starting to separate now,
sentences.zh: 所以，在总统图书馆的历史中以如此令人不适的方式混合在一起的两个目的，也许，你知道，它们现在开始分开了，

sentences.en: which is what seems like a good idea.
sentences.zh: 这看起来是个好主意。

sentences.en: But that brings us back to the question of the Trump library.
sentences.zh: 但这又让我们回到了特朗普图书馆的问题上。

sentences.en: And after hearing all this history, I kind of can't imagine any part of that not being filled with Trumpian nonsense.
sentences.zh: 在听了所有这些历史之后，我简直无法想象其中有哪一部分不会充斥着特朗普式的胡言乱语。

sentences.en: Yeah, I know.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我知道。

sentences.en: And that's that's what I meant at the beginning when I said that these libraries are all very Trumpian in a way.
sentences.zh: 这就是我一开始说这些图书馆在某种程度上都很“特朗普”的意思。

sentences.en: They all contain evasions and half-truths and bluster.
sentences.zh: 它们都包含逃避、半真半假的话和虚张声势。

sentences.en: And that's what our anonymous architect was thinking about, too, when on election night 2016, he was contemplating the idea of a future Trump library.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们那位匿名建筑师在2016年选举之夜思考未来特朗普图书馆时所想到的。

sentences.en: And what he did is he ended up buying a domain, djtrumplibrary.com.
sentences.zh: 他最终做的是买下了一个域名，djtrumplibrary.com。

sentences.en: And he just sat on that domain for a couple of years.
sentences.zh: 他在那个域名上坐等了几年。

sentences.en: But then he eventually decided, I am going to design a library that does exactly what none of these real presidential libraries do, which is to really dwell on the bad stuff.
sentences.zh: 但后来他最终决定，我要设计一个图书馆，做那些真正的总统图书馆都不做的事情，那就是真正深入探讨那些糟糕的事情。

sentences.en: Every president has faults.
sentences.zh: 每一位总统都有缺点。

sentences.en: It's a tough job.
sentences.zh: 这是一份艰难的工作。

sentences.en: I don't know why anybody wants a job that job sends lousy me.
sentences.zh: 我不知道为什么有人想要一份让人感到糟糕的工作。

sentences.en: But, you know, with Trump, there was just so much bad and so much scandal.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，对于特朗普，有太多的糟糕事和太多的丑闻了。

sentences.en: And so this guy designed a parody museum.
sentences.zh: 于是这家伙设计了一个恶搞博物馆。

sentences.en: And if you visit the site, it looks very much like a real presidential library.
sentences.zh: 如果你访问这个网站，它看起来非常像一个真正的总统图书馆。

sentences.en: It's a modern glass box.
sentences.zh: 它是一个现代化的玻璃盒子。

sentences.en: There's a reflecting pool and various exhibits.
sentences.zh: 有一个倒影池和各种展览。

sentences.en: But all of the exhibits are sort of fake parody exhibits.
sentences.zh: 但所有的展览都是某种虚假的恶搞展览。

sentences.en: There's a Twitter wall, for instance.
sentences.zh: 例如，有一个推特墙。

sentences.en: We had a room about the tax evasion numbers where he's only paying, I think it was like $750 a year.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个关于逃税数字的房间，他每年只交了，我想是750美元左右。

sentences.en: And then that was a room.
sentences.zh: 然后那成了一个房间。

sentences.en: We had the oligarchs lounge where it showed him kissing up to all the different despots and, you know, generally bad people.
sentences.zh: 我们有寡头休息室，展示了他如何讨好所有不同的独裁者，你知道，通常是坏人。

sentences.en: He likes the Putin's of the world, the Kim Jong-il's of the world, all these guys he's BFFs with.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢世界上的普京、金正日之流，所有这些他称兄道弟的家伙。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm starting to understand why this guy wanted to remain anonymous.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我开始明白为什么这家伙想保持匿名了。

sentences.en: Yeah, he just didn't feel entirely safe being public about who designed the site, which actually ended up getting a ton of attention.
sentences.zh: 是啊，他只是觉得公开自己设计了这个网站不太安全，而这个网站最终获得了巨大的关注。

sentences.en: For a long time, it was the first thing that came up when you Googled Donald Trump library.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间里，当你谷歌搜索“唐纳德·特朗普图书馆”时，它都是第一个跳出来的结果。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I haven't even heard of an official one.
sentences.zh: 我甚至没听说过有一个官方的。

sentences.en: Like, this is what I've heard of.
sentences.zh: 就像，这就是我听说过的。

sentences.en: It's this fake one.
sentences.zh: 就是这个假的。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's a lot of speculation about what a real one might look like, where it might be, if it will even exiSt.
sentences.zh: 是啊，关于一个真正的图书馆可能是什么样子、可能在哪里、甚至是否会存在，有很多猜测。

sentences.en: But the bigger point that this architect wanted to make isn't even necessarily about Trump.
sentences.zh: 但这位建筑师想要表达的更重要的观点甚至不一定关于特朗普。

sentences.en: It's more just about the way we think about presidents.
sentences.zh: 它更多是关于我们看待总统的方式。

sentences.en: It's a job.
sentences.zh: 这只是一份工作。

sentences.en: Like, the sooner we get to treating politicians as employees and not as heroes or people that we have to venerate for no good reason.
sentences.zh: 就像，我们越早把政客视为雇员，而不是英雄，或者不是那种我们无缘无故必须崇拜的人，就越好。

sentences.en: I mean, look, it's an important job, and they deserve our respect to their jobs well, but they're public employees.
sentences.zh: 我是说，看，这是一份重要的工作，如果他们工作出色，他们理应得到我们的尊重，但他们是公职人员。

sentences.en: They're replaceable.
sentences.zh: 他们是可以被替代的。

sentences.en: So I guess, in the end, this story is pretty much an episode of what Trump can teach us about presidential libraries.
sentences.zh: 所以我猜，最后，这个故事几乎就是“特朗普能教我们什么关于总统图书馆的知识”的一集。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's interesting that it took Trump, and before him, Nixon, to challenge the whole idea of presidential libraries.
sentences.zh: 是啊，有趣的是，直到特朗普，以及在他之前的尼克松，才挑战了总统图书馆的整个理念。

sentences.en: It's like he's helped expose some of the problems and contradictions that exist in all of them, even for the presidents that I tend to venerate.
sentences.zh: 就像他帮助揭露了所有这些图书馆中存在的一些问题和矛盾，即使是对于那些我倾向于崇拜的总统也是如此。

sentences.en: Right, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错，是啊。

sentences.en: It's like there was all this talk during the Trump era about how he exposed so many different institutions and conventions and traditions as inadequate or flawed.
sentences.zh: 就像在特朗普时代，人们一直在谈论他如何揭露了如此多不同的机构、惯例和传统，认为它们是不充分或有缺陷的。

sentences.en: And presidential libraries just feel like one more thing we can see in a new light now.
sentences.zh: 而总统图书馆感觉就像我们现在可以以一种新的眼光看待的又一件事物。

sentences.en: Well, what a weird collection of buildings.
sentences.zh: 嗯，真是奇怪的一系列建筑。

sentences.en: Well, thanks so much for bringing us this story.
sentences.zh: 好吧，非常感谢你给我们带来这个故事。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 不客气。

sentences.en: Thanks, Roman.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，罗曼。

sentences.en: Coming up after the break, we're going to share a recent episode of What Trump Can Teach Us About Con Law.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，我们将分享“特朗普能教我们什么关于宪法知识”的一期最新节目。

sentences.en: It's the other podcast I host with law professor Elizabeth Jo.
sentences.zh: 这是我和法学教授伊丽莎白·乔共同主持的另一个播客。

sentences.en: It covers the Supreme Court's shadow docket.
sentences.zh: 它涵盖了最高法院的“影子案卷”。

sentences.en: Stay tuned.
sentences.zh: 敬请期待。

sentences.en: And now an episode of What Trump Can Teach Us About Con Law, released on September 9th.
sentences.zh: 现在是9月9日发布的“特朗普能教我们什么关于宪法知识”的一期节目。

sentences.en: Okay, so we're recording this on Monday at 11.45 a.m.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们现在是在周一上午11点45分录制这期节目。

sentences.en: We're meeting as a sort of special session.
sentences.zh: 我们是以一种特别会议的形式会面。

sentences.en: So what do you want to talk about today?
sentences.zh: 那么你今天想谈些什么？

sentences.en: We're going to talk about legal procedure.
sentences.zh: 我们要谈谈法律程序。

sentences.en: I know that sounds really boring.
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来很无聊。

sentences.en: But I've learned not from you.
sentences.zh: 但我从你那里学到了，这并不无聊。

sentences.en: It won't be boring from you.
sentences.zh: 从你这里讲出来就不会无聊。

sentences.en: But I promise I'm going to show you why it's actually pretty interesting and maybe sometimes just as important or even more important than the right stuff that we talk about.
sentences.zh: 但我保证我会向你展示为什么它实际上非常有趣，有时甚至和我们谈论的那些权利问题一样重要，甚至更重要。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Cool.
sentences.zh: 酷。

sentences.en: So when we think about the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们想到美国最高法院，当它决定重要或特别有争议的问题时，我们谈论的是它所谓的“案情案卷”。

sentences.en: Supreme Court and when it decides important or in particularly controversial issues, what we're talking about is what's called its merits docket.
sentences.zh: 案卷只是指它的法律诉讼清单。

sentences.en: Docket just means its list of legal proceedings.
sentences.zh: 所以每年，确实有成千上万输掉官司的人请求最高法院审理他们的案件。

sentences.en: So every year, literally thousands of people who have lost their legal case ask the Supreme Court to hear their case.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这里发生的情况是有人输掉了一场官司，可能是民事或刑事案件，

sentences.en: You know, what's happened here is that somebody has lost a case, could be civil or criminal,
sentences.zh: 案件始于州法院或联邦法院，然后上诉到上诉法院，有时甚至上诉到州最高法院。

sentences.en: and the case started at state court or federal court and then went up to an appeals court and then sometimes even to a state Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 所以当败诉方说，“嘿，最高法院，请审理我的案件”时，很多法院已经发表过意见了。

sentences.en: And so by the time a losing party says, hey, Supreme Court, please hear my case, a lot of courts have already weighed in.
sentences.zh: 他们已经说，“你知道，我们已经做出了对你不利的判决”，或者在某些层面上他们说已经做出了对你有利的判决。

sentences.en: They've already said, you know, we've decided against you or maybe at some level they said they've decided for you.
sentences.zh: 但无论何时，当你到达最高法院时，你通常都是个失败者。

sentences.en: But at any point by the time you get to the Supreme Court, you're usually a loser.
sentences.zh: 你希望有人最后一次审理你的案件。

sentences.en: You want someone to hear your case one last time.
sentences.zh: 在成千上万的案件中，最高法院每年决定审理大约60到70起，所以数量并不多。

sentences.en: Of those thousands of cases, the Supreme Court decides to hear about 60 to 70 a year, so not that many.
sentences.zh: 当涉及到这类案件时，无论我们谈论的是个人权利还是联邦政府制定法律的权力，

sentences.en: And when it comes to those kinds of cases, whether we're talking about individual rights or the power of the federal government to make laws,
sentences.zh: 最高法院会让双方提交通常两轮的法律摘要。

sentences.en: the Supreme Court has the two sides submit usually two rounds of legal briefs.
sentences.zh: 这些是关于他们为什么应该胜诉的书面论点。

sentences.en: These are written arguments about why they should win.
sentences.zh: 然后会有一个提前几个月安排好的口头辩论。

sentences.en: And then there's an oral argument that's scheduled months in advance.
sentences.zh: 当涉及到非常引人注目的案件时，也就是我们都在报纸上读到的那些案件，你可能还会收到几份“法庭之友”摘要。

sentences.en: When it comes to really high profile cases, the ones that we all read about in the newspapers, you might also get several amicus or friend of the court briefs.
sentences.zh: 这些是由非案件当事方撰写的法律摘要，但他们是在告诉最高法院，“嘿，这是一个如此重要的问题”。

sentences.en: These are legal briefs that are written by the parties who aren't part of the case, but they're telling the Supreme Court, hey, this is such an important issue.
sentences.zh: “请也让我们发表意见吧”。

sentences.en: Please let us weigh in, too.
sentences.zh: 现在，在疫情之前，如果你幸运的话，你实际上可以排队买票，坐下来观看大法官们会问双方律师什么问题。

sentences.en: Now, before the pandemic, if you were lucky, you could actually wait in line and get a seat and watch what the justices were going to be asking of the lawyers for both sides.
sentences.zh: 现在，在疫情期间，我们在这方面其实还算幸运。

sentences.en: Now, during the pandemic, we're actually kind of lucky in this regard.
sentences.zh: 他们转到了线上，或者说是某种程度上的线上。

sentences.en: They went online or sort of online.
sentences.zh: 他们通过电话转到了线上。

sentences.en: They went telephonically online.
sentences.zh: 他们通过电话转到了线上。

sentences.en: And so we could hear what the justices were asking the different parties during this last term.
sentences.zh: 这样我们就能听到大法官们在上个任期里向各方提出了什么问题。

sentences.en: Eventually, the Supreme Court decides how the case is supposed to come out.
sentences.zh: 最终，最高法院会决定案件的判决结果。

sentences.en: And there's usually a lengthy written opinion signed by the justice who actually authored the opinion.
sentences.zh: 通常会有一份冗长的书面意见书，由实际撰写该意见的大法官签署。

sentences.en: And we can tell which justices agreed with the majority opinion.
sentences.zh: 我们也能看出哪些大法官同意多数派意见。

sentences.en: And if there are those who didn't agree, well, then you have these dissents, right?
sentences.zh: 如果有人不同意，那么就会有异议意见，对吧？

sentences.en: Dissenting justices say, well, this is why I think the majority is wrong and we should have done something different.
sentences.zh: 持异议的大法官会说，这就是为什么我认为多数派错了，我们本应该采取不同的做法。

sentences.en: So that's the Supreme Court we all know and love.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们所熟知和喜爱的最高法院。

sentences.en: The one that I've just called the merits docket.
sentences.zh: 也就是我刚才所说的“案情审理卷宗”。

sentences.en: That's the one where we hear about the big blockbuster cases.
sentences.zh: 我们听到的那些重磅大案就是指这些。

sentences.en: So this whole process, like waiting, usually waiting until the end of the summer to see what the Supreme Court is going to say in a particularly important case.
sentences.zh: 所以整个过程，比如等待，通常要等到夏末才能看到最高法院对一个特别重要的案件会做出什么裁决。

sentences.en: Well, the reason why we have all of this incredible procedure and people weighing in and there's all this pomp and circumstance, that's kind of the court's legitimacy.
sentences.zh: 之所以我们有所有这些令人难以置信的程序，有各方参与，还有所有这些礼仪和排场，某种程度上就是为了法院的合法性。

sentences.en: They don't just decide.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅仅是做出决定。

sentences.en: They don't flip a coin.
sentences.zh: 他们不会掷硬币来决定。

sentences.en: They don't say, hey, we were voted in by this president, so that's how we're going to decide.
sentences.zh: 他们不会说，嘿，我们是由这位总统任命的，所以我们就该这么判。

sentences.en: They're supposed to say, here's the lengthy legal reasoning behind why we're going to go ahead and say the case should come out in a particular way.
sentences.zh: 他们理应说，这就是我们决定以特定方式判决此案背后的冗长法律推理。

sentences.en: And the idea here is that because we've handed over to the Supreme Court so much power to decide sometimes really life-altering decisions in the lives of ordinary people,
sentences.zh: 这里的理念是，因为我们将如此巨大的权力交给了最高法院，让其决定有时会彻底改变普通人生活的大事，

sentences.en: they owe it to us as the public to explain why they're doing what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 他们有义务向我们公众解释他们为什么这样做。

sentences.en: But that's not everything the Supreme Court does.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是最高法院所做的全部工作。

sentences.en: It also has what's referred to as a non-merits or emotions docket.
sentences.zh: 它还有所谓的“非案情审理卷宗”或“动议卷宗”。

sentences.en: So, Roman, have you ever heard of that term?
sentences.zh: 那么，罗曼，你听说过这个术语吗？

sentences.en: No, not at all.
sentences.zh: 没有，完全没听过。

sentences.en: Never, right?
sentences.zh: 从来没听过，对吧？

sentences.en: And really, nobody ever has, unless you practice regularly before the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 说实话，除非你经常在最高法院执业，否则没人听说过。

sentences.en: You've never heard of this term.
sentences.zh: 你从来没听说过这个术语。

sentences.en: And the reason why is it's usually pretty boring.
sentences.zh: 原因在于它通常相当枯燥。

sentences.en: Now, the reason why there's a non-merits or emotions docket is that the Supreme Court, like any other court, has to issue a lot of orders.
sentences.zh: 现在，之所以存在非案情审理卷宗或动议卷宗，是因为最高法院像任何其他法院一样，必须发布大量的命令。

sentences.en: Sometimes the parties in a case want to do something kind of boring, like, hey, can we have more time to file a brief?
sentences.zh: 有时案件当事人想做一些比较琐碎的事情，比如，嘿，我们能多要点时间提交简报吗？

sentences.en: Or sometimes the Supreme Court says, hey, you folks, you wanted an emergency order?
sentences.zh: 或者有时最高法院会说，嘿，各位，你们想要紧急命令？

sentences.en: There's no emergency here.
sentences.zh: 这里根本没有紧急情况。

sentences.en: Or you want us to hear your case?
sentences.zh: 或者你们想让我们审理你们的案子？

sentences.en: It's just not that important.
sentences.zh: 这案子没那么重要。

sentences.en: So for all these kinds of reasons, this non-motions or orders docket never gets any attention.
sentences.zh: 所以由于所有这些原因，这个非案情审理或命令卷宗从来没有得到任何关注。

sentences.en: I shouldn't say never.
sentences.zh: 我不该说从来没有。

sentences.en: Very occasionally, you might hear of a death penalty case, where there's been a death row inmate facing execution,
sentences.zh: 偶尔你可能会听说死刑案件，有死囚面临处决，

sentences.en: and the Supreme Court in that case might be asked to issue a stay, or that's really like a pause of the execution,
sentences.zh: 最高法院在那种情况下可能会被要求发布暂缓执行令，那实际上就像是暂停执行，

sentences.en: because that person argues that there's some constitutional problem in their case.
sentences.zh: 因为那个人辩称他们的案件存在某种宪法问题。

sentences.en: But again, most of the time, the non-merits docket of the Supreme Court is pretty unexciting, and really no one's ever heard of it.
sentences.zh: 但再说一次，大多数时候，最高法院的非案情审理卷宗相当乏味，而且真的没人听说过它。

sentences.en: But in recent years, that boring part of the Supreme Court's work has gotten a lot more interesting, and in ways that a lot of people find alarming.
sentences.zh: 但近年来，最高法院工作中那部分枯燥的内容变得有趣多了，而且是以许多人感到惊恐的方式。

sentences.en: So let's talk about the shadow docket, abortion in Texas, and maybe the state of abortion rights everywhere.
sentences.zh: 所以我们来谈谈“影子卷宗”、德克萨斯州的堕胎问题，以及堕胎权在各地的现状。

sentences.en: Let's do it.
sentences.zh: 我们开始吧。

sentences.en: This is What Trump Can Teach Us About Con Law, an ongoing series of indefinite length, where we take the horrible current events and the ripple effects of the Trump presidency,
sentences.zh: 这是《特朗普能教我们什么宪法知识》，一个长度不限的持续系列节目，我们选取特朗普总统任期内可怕的时事及其连锁反应，

sentences.en: and use them to examine our constitution like we never have before.
sentences.zh: 并利用它们以前所未有的方式来审视我们的宪法。

sentences.en: Our music is from Doomtree Records, our professor and neighbor is Elizabeth Jo, and I'm your fellow perpetual student and host, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我们的音乐来自 Doomtree Records，我们的教授和邻居是伊丽莎白·乔，我是你们的终身学生同伴兼主持人，罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: So I've heard this term on Twitter a little bit, and I'm here to ask, what is a shadow docket?
sentences.zh: 我在推特上听到过这个术语，所以我来问问，什么是“影子卷宗”？

sentences.en: Okay, so the actual term is something coined by a law professor named Will Bode in 2015 to describe what we've just talked about,
sentences.zh: 好的，这个术语实际上是由一位名叫威尔·博德的法学教授在2015年创造的，用来描述我们刚才谈到的内容，

sentences.en: this idea of an orders docket of the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 也就是最高法院的命令卷宗这一概念。

sentences.en: Even though the term's coined pretty recently, the Supreme Court's always had this thing where they just have to issue orders that are related to cases before them.
sentences.zh: 尽管这个术语是最近才创造出来的，但最高法院一直都有这种做法，即他们必须发布与审理案件相关的命令。

sentences.en: Again, historically, pretty boring.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，从历史上看，这相当枯燥。

sentences.en: No one usually cares about it.
sentences.zh: 通常没人关心它。

sentences.en: But if you're a watcher of the Supreme Court, you've probably noticed that in recent years,
sentences.zh: 但如果你是最高法院的观察者，你可能已经注意到，近年来，

sentences.en: the Supreme Court seems to be relying more on the so-called shadow docket to make decisions in high-profile cases.
sentences.zh: 最高法院似乎越来越依赖所谓的“影子卷宗”来对备受瞩目的案件做出裁决。

sentences.en: So you ask, why is it a shadow docket?
sentences.zh: 所以你问，为什么叫“影子卷宗”？

sentences.en: What is it?
sentences.zh: 它是什么？

sentences.en: So these are not the ordinary way that the Supreme Court decides cases.
sentences.zh: 这些并不是最高法院审理案件的常规方式。

sentences.en: There's no extensive rounds of legal briefing.
sentences.zh: 没有广泛的法律简报环节。

sentences.en: There's no oral arguments by the lawyers.
sentences.zh: 没有律师的口头辩论。

sentences.en: There's no oral argument decided in advance months ahead of time for all of us to try and figure out if we can attend in person or maybe listen to online.
sentences.zh: 没有提前几个月就决定好的口头辩论，让我们所有人去弄清楚是否可以亲自参加或在线收听。

sentences.en: The Supreme Court might just issue an order.
sentences.zh: 最高法院可能只是发布一道命令。

sentences.en: Sometimes there's no legal opinion, or there's just a very brief opinion.
sentences.zh: 有时没有法律意见书，或者只有一份非常简短的意见书。

sentences.en: It might be one paragraph long.
sentences.zh: 可能只有一段话那么长。

sentences.en: And the court's usually on a really rushed timeline.
sentences.zh: 而且法院通常处于非常仓促的时间表下。

sentences.en: And sometimes we don't really know which justice wrote the opinion.
sentences.zh: 有时我们真的不知道是哪位大法官撰写的意见书。

sentences.en: And sometimes we don't really know which justices totally agreed with that unsigned opinion.
sentences.zh: 有时我们真的不知道哪些大法官完全同意那份未署名的意见书。

sentences.en: And they can decide these orders at any time they wish.
sentences.zh: 而且他们可以在他们希望的任何时间决定这些命令。

sentences.en: Could be in the middle of the night.
sentences.zh: 可能是在半夜。

sentences.en: So you can see that this is really different than the way that the court normally decides its cases.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看出，这与法院通常审理案件的方式确实不同。

sentences.en: And that's kind of the problem.
sentences.zh: 而这正是问题所在。

sentences.en: It's less transparent.
sentences.zh: 它透明度较低。

sentences.en: It's less predictable.
sentences.zh: 它可预测性较差。

sentences.en: The parties themselves aren't that much involved in these cases.
sentences.zh: 当事人本身并没有过多参与这些案件。

sentences.en: So the whole idea is that they're just kind of less open overall when it comes to the shadow docket.
sentences.zh: 所以整个想法是，在“影子卷宗”方面，他们总体上没那么开放。

sentences.en: And when you have something as important as the Supreme Court, remember, practically speaking, they have the final say on what the Constitution means.
sentences.zh: 当你拥有像最高法院这样重要的机构时，请记住，实际上，他们对宪法的含义拥有最终解释权。

sentences.en: That raises issues about their trustworthiness and their legitimacy if they're issuing really big decisions in the middle of the night.
sentences.zh: 如果他们在半夜发布非常重大的决定，这就会引发关于他们可信度和合法性的问题。

sentences.en: And we're not even sure who wrote the thing that makes such a big impression.
sentences.zh: 而且我们甚至不确定是谁写了那份产生如此大影响的文件。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So you and I just talked about a shadow docket case pretty recently.
sentences.zh: 所以你和我最近刚谈过一个“影子卷宗”案件。

sentences.en: And that was one of the COVID cases.
sentences.zh: 那就是其中一个新冠疫情相关的案件。

sentences.en: Remember, there was a challenge to the COVID restrictions in New York State.
sentences.zh: 还记得吗，当时有人对纽约州的新冠防疫限制措施提出了质疑。

sentences.en: And just as a recap, remember,
sentences.zh: 简单回顾一下，请记住，

sentences.en: some religious groups said that the state of New York was treating them more harshly than if you were a non-religious entity when it came to allowing people for indoor gatherings.
sentences.zh: 一些宗教团体表示，在允许人们进行室内聚会时，纽约州对待他们比对待非宗教实体更严厉。

sentences.en: So the Supreme Court decided in that case, remember, that on the midnight before Thanksgiving of last year, that, yep,
sentences.zh: 所以最高法院在那个案件中裁定，请记住，在去年感恩节的前一天午夜，是的，

sentences.en: this was an unconstitutional restriction on their religious freedom.
sentences.zh: 这是对他们宗教自由的违宪限制。

sentences.en: That COVID restriction, even though, of course, there was a public health reason behind it, violated their First Amendment religious freedom rights.
sentences.zh: 尽管那项新冠限制措施背后当然有公共卫生原因，但它违反了他们第一修正案中的宗教自由权利。

sentences.en: This is an example of a shadow docket decision.
sentences.zh: 这就是“影子卷宗”裁决的一个例子。

sentences.en: This wasn't an ordinary case with the oral arguments and the briefing.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个有口头辩论和简报的普通案件。

sentences.en: In fact, it was an emergency request by the religious groups.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这是宗教团体提出的紧急请求。

sentences.en: And the Supreme Court intervened and said, oh, you can't do this, New York.
sentences.zh: 最高法院进行了干预并说，哦，纽约，你们不能这样做。

sentences.en: That was a 5-4 opinion.
sentences.zh: 那是一份5比4的意见书。

sentences.en: It was unsigned.
sentences.zh: 它是未署名的。

sentences.en: And we know the vote in this particular case because there were four justices who dissented, including the Chief Justice, John Roberts.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这个特定案件的投票结果，因为有四位大法官表示异议，包括首席大法官约翰·罗伯茨。

sentences.en: There are plenty of other examples, too.
sentences.zh: 还有很多其他的例子。

sentences.en: So do you remember the eviction moratorium that Congress imposed at the early part of the pandemic?
sentences.zh: 那么你还记得国会在疫情初期实施的驱逐禁令吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然记得。

sentences.en: So you have this idea where Congress stopped evictions as part of the second COVID Relief Act.
sentences.zh: 所以你有这样一个概念，国会作为第二次新冠救济法案的一部分停止了驱逐行为。

sentences.en: And the idea here is, of course, if you have mass unemployment because of COVID, that leads to people being homeless, and maybe that would make the pandemic even worse.
sentences.zh: 这里的想法当然是，如果你因为新冠疫情而大规模失业，这会导致人们无家可归，也许这会让疫情变得更糟。

sentences.en: When Congress decides to impose this moratorium, it was supposed to last just 120 days, and Congress decides not to renew it.
sentences.zh: 当国会决定实施这项禁令时，它本应只持续120天，而国会决定不再续期。

sentences.en: But the Centers for Disease Control, CDC, was concerned that, well, maybe there still should be an eviction moratorium.
sentences.zh: 但疾病控制与预防中心（CDC）担心，嗯，也许还是应该有驱逐禁令。

sentences.en: So they decide on their own to extend the moratorium a couple of times.
sentences.zh: 所以他们自行决定将禁令延长了几次。

sentences.en: So that CDC moratorium was challenged in federal court.
sentences.zh: 因此，CDC的这项禁令在联邦法院受到了挑战。

sentences.en: A federal judge agreed that, well, maybe the CDC doesn't have the authority to do this, but, you know, we'll put a pause on this decision while the parties appeal.
sentences.zh: 一位联邦法官同意，嗯，也许CDC没有权力这样做，但是，你知道，在当事人上诉期间，我们会暂停这项决定。

sentences.en: So eventually this goes up as kind of another emergency decision to the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 所以最终这作为另一个紧急决定上诉到了最高法院。

sentences.en: So remember when you think about the importance of an eviction moratorium, like, you know, what's the public interest here, do you think?
sentences.zh: 所以当你想到驱逐禁令的重要性时，比如，你知道，你认为这里的公共利益是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, I would say the public interest is really high because it's a matter of life and death if you have a home or not.
sentences.zh: 是的，我会说公共利益非常高，因为是否有家可归是生死攸关的问题。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it's something that potentially affects hundreds of thousands of people, right?
sentences.zh: 而且这可能影响成千上万的人，对吧？

sentences.en: People who are just on the brink of eviction.
sentences.zh: 那些正处于被驱逐边缘的人们。

sentences.en: So when you think about it just in terms of, like, ordinary folks, ordinary Americans being affected by this, this kind of feels like a case that normally,
sentences.zh: 所以当你从普通人、受此影响的普通美国人的角度来考虑时，这感觉就像是一个通常，

sentences.en: shouldn't it be part of the court's normal caseload?
sentences.zh: 难道不应该成为法院正常审理案件的一部分吗？

sentences.en: We have briefs, you have an oral argument, maybe you accept a dozen in front of the court briefs, maybe there should be a really lengthy opinion about a really big question.
sentences.zh: 我们有简报，有口头辩论，也许你在法院面前接受十几份简报，也许应该有一份关于一个非常重大问题的非常冗长的意见书。

sentences.en: You know, can a federal agency that's responsible for stopping communicable diseases,
sentences.zh: 你知道，一个负责阻止传染病的联邦机构，

sentences.en: can they have an eviction moratorium as one of those measures during a global unprecedented pandemic?
sentences.zh: 他们能否在全球前所未有的疫情期间将驱逐禁令作为这些措施之一？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But instead, this is a shadow docket case.
sentences.zh: 但相反，这是一个“影子卷宗”案件。

sentences.en: So on August 26th, the court issued an opinion, a short one, eight pages, it's unsigned.
sentences.zh: 所以8月26日，法院发布了一份意见书，很短，八页，未署名。

sentences.en: They say, no, the CDC can't do this.
sentences.zh: 他们说，不，CDC不能这样做。

sentences.en: And so no more eviction moratorium.
sentences.zh: 所以驱逐禁令不再有效。

sentences.en: Justice Breyer wrote a dissenting opinion, not just about the substance of the decision, but the procedure.
sentences.zh: 布雷耶大法官写了一份异议意见书，不仅是关于裁决的实质内容，还有程序问题。

sentences.en: He says, these questions call for considered decision-making, informed by full briefing and argument.
sentences.zh: 他说，这些问题需要经过深思熟虑的决策，并以充分的简报和辩论为依据。

sentences.en: Their answers impact the health of millions.
sentences.zh: 它们的答案影响着数百万人的健康。

sentences.en: We should not set aside the CDC's eviction moratorium in this summary proceeding.
sentences.zh: 我们不应该在这种简易程序中搁置CDC的驱逐禁令。

sentences.en: So Breyer is really saying, I don't like this, and I also don't like the way we're doing this.
sentences.zh: 所以布雷耶实际上是在说，我不喜欢这样，我也不喜欢我们这样做的方式。

sentences.en: We need to have this in a regular, transparent, open way that we do with our other really big cases.
sentences.zh: 我们需要以我们处理其他重大案件时那种常规、透明、公开的方式来处理这个问题。

sentences.en: So this is a roundabout way of getting to the more recent news, and that is the Texas law, right, SP8.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个绕弯子引出最近新闻的方式，那就是德克萨斯州的法律，对吧，SP8法案。

sentences.en: So let's talk about that.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈那个。

sentences.en: In May, the governor of Texas, Greg Abbott, he signs SP8 into law.
sentences.zh: 五月，德克萨斯州州长格雷格·阿博特签署了SP8法案使其成为法律。

sentences.en: The law is actually pretty similar to a number of other state abortion laws that are called heartbeat laws.
sentences.zh: 该法律实际上与其他一些被称为“心跳法案”的州堕胎法非常相似。

sentences.en: So basically, this new law says that women in Texas can obtain illegal abortion when you can detect a fetal heartbeat, which is around six weeks of pregnancy.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，这项新法律规定，当能检测到胎儿心跳时，德克萨斯州的女性可以获得非法堕胎，这大约是在怀孕六周时。

sentences.en: But six weeks just means that almost all abortions are banned because at six weeks, many women have no idea that they're pregnant.
sentences.zh: 但六周意味着几乎所有的堕胎都被禁止了，因为在六周时，许多女性根本不知道自己怀孕了。

sentences.en: So if I say, look, other states have done this before, well, it also means that other states, when they've had such laws, they've been challenged in court,
sentences.zh: 所以如果我说，看，其他州以前也这样做过，嗯，这也意味着其他州在有此类法律时，它们在法庭上受到了挑战，

sentences.en: and they've generally been struck down because these laws violate a woman's constitutional rights.
sentences.zh: 而且它们通常被推翻了，因为这些法律侵犯了女性的宪法权利。

sentences.en: You and I have talked a couple of times about Roe v.
sentences.zh: 你和我谈过几次罗诉韦德案，

sentences.en: Wade and how the Supreme Court has interpreted what the states can do.
sentences.zh: 以及最高法院如何解释各州可以做什么。

sentences.en: But just as a refresher, remember, states are not allowed to completely ban abortion before what's called fetal viability.
sentences.zh: 但作为复习，请记住，各州不允许在所谓的“胎儿存活能力”之前完全禁止堕胎。

sentences.en: That means the stage when a fetus can live outside of the womb.
sentences.zh: 这意味着胎儿可以在子宫外存活的阶段。

sentences.en: That's why previous six-week bans are easily struck down.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么以前的六周禁令很容易被推翻。

sentences.en: Six weeks is way, way, way before the point of viability.
sentences.zh: 六周远在存活点之前。

sentences.en: Okay, so SP8.
sentences.zh: 好的，那么SP8法案。

sentences.en: The Texas law, though, is different in kind of a devious and dastardly way.
sentences.zh: 然而，德克萨斯州的法律在某种阴险和卑鄙的方式上有所不同。

sentences.en: Okay, we've talked about Roe v.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们之前谈过罗诉韦德案，

sentences.en: Wade before, and the story behind Jane Roe, who was later identified as Norma McCorvey.
sentences.zh: 以及简·罗背后的故事，她后来被确认为诺玛·麦考维。

sentences.en: Now, let's look at it in a different way.
sentences.zh: 现在，让我们从不同的角度来看它。

sentences.en: The case is called Roe v.
sentences.zh: 这个案子叫罗诉韦德案，对吧？

sentences.en: Wade, right?
sentences.zh: 我们花了很多时间谈论简·罗。

sentences.en: We spent a lot of time talking about Jane Roe.
sentences.zh: 那么，韦德是谁？

sentences.en: Well, who's Wade?
sentences.zh: 思考这个问题的一部分是思考罗诉韦德案中被挑战的法律是什么，以及它是如何被挑战的。

sentences.en: Part of thinking about this is thinking about how the law challenged in Roe, what it was, and how it was challenged.
sentences.zh: 所以，在罗诉韦德案本身中，被挑战的法律之一规定获取堕胎服务是犯罪。

sentences.en: So, in Roe itself, one of the laws that was challenged made it a crime to procure an abortion.
sentences.zh: 所以，罗曼，如果某事是犯罪，谁来执行法律？

sentences.en: So, Roman, if something's a crime, who enforces the law?
sentences.zh: 地方检察官。

sentences.en: The district attorney.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, at the time of the law, of the challenge, Jane Roe was living in Dallas County, Texas.
sentences.zh: 在法律挑战发生时，简·罗（Jane Roe）住在德克萨斯州的达拉斯县。

sentences.en: And Wade is Henry Wade.
sentences.zh: 而韦德（Wade）指的是亨利·韦德（Henry Wade）。

sentences.en: He was the district attorney of Dallas County.
sentences.zh: 他当时是达拉斯县的地区检察官。

sentences.en: So, in other words, the person who, in theory, would be responsible for prosecuting violations of a criminal abortion statute.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他理论上是负责起诉违反刑事堕胎法规行为的人。

sentences.en: So, that's Wade.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是韦德。

sentences.en: That's the other party in the case who normally doesn't get any attention at all.
sentences.zh: 他是案件中的另一方，通常根本不会受到任何关注。

sentences.en: But this way, this procedure, the way the law is challenged, is pretty typical of a lot of lawsuits when it comes to constitutional rights.
sentences.zh: 但这种方式，这种程序，即法律被挑战的方式，在涉及宪法权利的诉讼中是非常典型的。

sentences.en: Someone sues because they argue that a law violates their rights under the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 有人提起诉讼，是因为他们认为某项法律违反了宪法赋予他们的权利。

sentences.en: And in order to do that, they often sue the person who's responsible for enforcing the law.
sentences.zh: 为了做到这一点，他们通常会起诉负责执行该法律的人。

sentences.en: So, if a court agrees that the law is unconstitutional, they're also deciding that that government official, so Henry Wade and Roe v.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果法院同意该法律违宪，他们同时也判定该政府官员——也就是亨利·韦德，以及在“罗诉韦德案”中，

sentences.en: Wade, who's standing in for all the other government officials, can't enforce an unconstitutional law.
sentences.zh: 代表所有其他政府官员的韦德——不能执行违宪的法律。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, Texas.
sentences.zh: 那么，德克萨斯州。

sentences.en: But Texas's law is different.
sentences.zh: 但德克萨斯州的法律有所不同。

sentences.en: The Texas law actually forbids the state's government officials from enforcing the law.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯州的法律实际上禁止了该州政府官员执行该法。

sentences.en: And instead, the law gives everybody else, any private person, the ability to sue.
sentences.zh: 相反，该法律赋予了其他人，即任何私人，起诉的权利。

sentences.en: But what can they sue for in this case?
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，他们能起诉什么呢？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, the first part maybe makes sense.
sentences.zh: 第一部分可能还说得通。

sentences.en: They can sue anybody who performs an abortion.
sentences.zh: 他们可以起诉任何进行堕胎手术的人。

sentences.en: But there's more.
sentences.zh: 但还有更多。

sentences.en: You can also sue, as a private individual, anyone who aids or abets an abortion.
sentences.zh: 作为私人，你还可以起诉任何协助或教唆堕胎的人。

sentences.en: Aids or abets is just a legal term for meaning helping.
sentences.zh: “协助或教唆”只是一个法律术语，意思就是帮忙。

sentences.en: So, anybody who helps.
sentences.zh: 所以，任何帮忙的人都可以被起诉。

sentences.en: But there's also more.
sentences.zh: 但还不止于此。

sentences.en: You can also sue anybody who intends to aid or abet an abortion.
sentences.zh: 你还可以起诉任何意图协助或教唆堕胎的人。

sentences.en: Whoa.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Or intends to perform an abortion.
sentences.zh: 或者意图进行堕胎手术的人。

sentences.en: So, that really means that because of SB8, which is structured in this really different way, you can sue an abortion provider.
sentences.zh: 所以，这实际上意味着由于SB8法案的这种特殊结构，你可以起诉堕胎服务提供者。

sentences.en: But you can also sue a friend or a family member, maybe who helped pay for your abortion.
sentences.zh: 但你也可以起诉你的朋友或家人，也许是那些帮你支付堕胎费用的人。

sentences.en: Maybe the Uber driver who drove you to the abortion services provider.
sentences.zh: 也许是那个开车送你去堕胎服务机构的优步司机。

sentences.en: Maybe your friend or family member who decided to drive you there on their own provided some source of support.
sentences.zh: 也许是你的朋友或家人，他们决定开车送你去那里，并提供了某种支持。

sentences.en: So, this is how this particular law, SB8, makes it really different in terms of raising a constitutional challenge.
sentences.zh: 这就是这项特殊的法律SB8在提出宪法挑战方面显得如此不同的原因。

sentences.en: So, my question is, who would be the hypothetical person suing here?
sentences.zh: 所以，我的问题是，这里假设的起诉人会是谁？

sentences.en: And why would they have standing to sue in this case, in any case?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们在这种情况下，或者在任何情况下，会有起诉资格？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, standing in terms of what the federal courts do comes from restrictions in the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 联邦法院所说的“起诉资格”源于宪法中的限制。

sentences.en: But this is a state law.
sentences.zh: 但这是一项州法律。

sentences.en: And states can define standing in different and sometimes wider ways.
sentences.zh: 各州可以以不同且有时更广泛的方式定义起诉资格。

sentences.en: So, it's a little bit unclear right now.
sentences.zh: 所以，目前还不完全清楚。

sentences.en: But it looks like, you know, Texas can allow citizens to have this kind of broad standing in ways that federal courts can't.
sentences.zh: 但看起来，德克萨斯州可以允许公民拥有联邦法院所无法提供的这种广泛的起诉资格。

sentences.en: But to get to your more specific question, who can sue?
sentences.zh: 但回到你更具体的问题，谁可以起诉？

sentences.en: Pretty much anybody.
sentences.zh: 几乎任何人。

sentences.en: You don't have to be a person in Texas.
sentences.zh: 你不必是德克萨斯州的人。

sentences.en: You can be presumably anybody on the planet.
sentences.zh: 据推测，你可以是地球上的任何人。

sentences.en: You just have to sue in a Texas court.
sentences.zh: 你只需要在德克萨斯州的法院提起诉讼即可。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And then sue for what?
sentences.zh: 然后起诉什么呢？

sentences.en: For the existence of abortion services?
sentences.zh: 起诉堕胎服务的存在？

sentences.en: Or sue for, sue whom?
sentences.zh: 还是起诉……起诉谁？

sentences.en: Like, I get that it can be anybody.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我明白可以是任何人。

sentences.en: You mentioned anybody in the process.
sentences.zh: 你提到了过程中的任何人。

sentences.en: So, I could just randomly pick out a person who got an abortion and then sue all the people that were involved in it.
sentences.zh: 所以我可以随便挑一个做过堕胎手术的人，然后起诉所有参与其中的人。

sentences.en: Like, just me as a person.
sentences.zh: 就像，以我个人的名义。

sentences.en: That seems to be the way it works.
sentences.zh: 这似乎就是它的运作方式。

sentences.en: So, basically, the state of Texas has shifted enforcement from, normally, you know, the way a crime works.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，德克萨斯州已经将执法权从通常的犯罪处理方式中转移了出来。

sentences.en: You'd have, again, the district attorneys, right, involved in prosecution.
sentences.zh: 通常会有地区检察官参与起诉，对吧？

sentences.en: This isn't a crime.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是犯罪。

sentences.en: This is basically handing over enforcement civilly to everybody else except people who normally enforce criminal laws.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是将民事执法权移交给了除通常执行刑事法律的人员之外的所有人。

sentences.en: And it does so by incentivizing these civil suits.
sentences.zh: 它通过激励这些民事诉讼来实现这一点。

sentences.en: If you sue and win, let's say you sue an abortion services provider, you sue someone who helped a woman obtain an abortion,
sentences.zh: 如果你起诉并胜诉，比如说你起诉了一家堕胎服务提供者，或者起诉了一个帮助女性堕胎的人，

sentences.en: you get to collect a minimum of $10,000 in attorney's fees for each abortion.
sentences.zh: 你每次堕胎至少可以获得1万美元的律师费。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And bizarrely, under the law, if you bring that lawsuit and lose, nothing happens to you.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，根据法律，如果你提起诉讼却败诉了，你也不会受到任何惩罚。

sentences.en: There's not only a penalty or anything.
sentences.zh: 甚至连罚款都没有。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: So, presumably, the result of this is every anti-abortion, you know, organization in the world could just begin suing.
sentences.zh: 所以，推测的结果是，世界上每一个反堕胎组织都可以开始起诉。

sentences.en: As long as they have, like, the facts of an abortion that has happened, they could just begin suing every part of the chain of provider, including the Lyft driver,
sentences.zh: 只要他们掌握了已经发生的堕胎事实，他们就可以开始起诉堕胎链条上的每一个环节，包括Lyft司机，

sentences.en: out of existence.
sentences.zh: 直到把他们赶尽杀绝。

sentences.en: That's what it sounds like.
sentences.zh: 听起来就是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, the law has just gone into effect as of September 1st, so we don't really know how it's going to work out.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，法律在9月1日才刚刚生效，所以我们还不知道它会如何运作。

sentences.en: But the financial incentive does feel like bounty hunting.
sentences.zh: 但这种经济激励确实感觉像赏金猎人。
