sentences.en: The whole scheme feels like kind of like legal trolling.
sentences.zh: 整个方案感觉就像一种法律骚扰。

sentences.en: You can just harass nearly anybody who is somehow connected with an abortion.
sentences.zh: 你可以骚扰几乎任何与堕胎有关的人。

sentences.en: If you're an abortion services provider, you either close down or you face a flood of civil lawsuits.
sentences.zh: 如果你是堕胎服务提供者，你要么关门大吉，要么面临如潮水般的民事诉讼。

sentences.en: And if you're an ordinary person who might formerly in Texas have been happy to help a friend or a family member, I think you're certainly deterred from doing so.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个普通人，以前在德克萨斯州可能很乐意帮助朋友或家人，我想你现在肯定会被吓得不敢再这么做了。

sentences.en: I mean, $10,000 is a lot of money, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，1万美元可是一大笔钱，对吧？

sentences.en: $10,000 is a lot to be liable for.
sentences.zh: 1万美元的赔偿责任可不是小数目。

sentences.en: So, after the law is enacted, a group of abortion services providers in Texas then filed a lawsuit.
sentences.zh: 所以，在该法律颁布后，德克萨斯州的一群堕胎服务提供者提起了一项诉讼。

sentences.en: That's not surprising.
sentences.zh: 这并不令人惊讶。

sentences.en: They filed a lawsuit in federal court in July to try and stop the law from taking effect, which was designed to go into effect on September 1St.
sentences.zh: 他们在7月份向联邦法院提起诉讼，试图阻止该法律生效，该法律原定于9月1日生效。

sentences.en: So, Roman, we did talk about how SB8 is different than, say, the law that was challenged in Roe v.
sentences.zh: 那么，罗曼，我们确实讨论过SB8与“罗诉韦德案”中被挑战的法律有何不同。

sentences.en: Wade.
sentences.zh: 那么，你能看出这个诉讼的问题所在吗？

sentences.en: So, can you see the problem here with the lawsuit?
sentences.zh: 嗯，没有“韦德”。

sentences.en: Well, there's no Wade.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没有韦德。

sentences.en: There's no Wade.
sentences.zh: 你要起诉谁？

sentences.en: Who do you sue?
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 所以，这确实是个问题。

sentences.en: So, that's a bit of a problem.
sentences.zh: 在这个特定的诉讼中，他们起诉了一名州法官、一名代表全体州法官和书记官的书记官，以及一名据推测是反堕胎的私人。

sentences.en: So, in this particular lawsuit, they sue a state judge, a clerk on behalf of a whole class of state judges and clerks, and a private individual who is presumably anti-abortion.
sentences.zh: 现在记住，你刚才说没有韦德，因为他们无法起诉韦德。

sentences.en: Now, remember, you just said there's no Wade because they can't sue a Wade.
sentences.zh: 他们无法起诉德克萨斯州的地区检察官或任何其他州行政官员，因为法律实际上说，你知道的，

sentences.en: They can't sue a district attorney or any other state executive official in Texas because the law actually says, you know,
sentences.zh: 这些政府官员不负责执行这项法律。

sentences.en: these government officials aren't responsible for enforcing this law.
sentences.zh: 其他人负责。

sentences.en: Everybody else is.
sentences.zh: 所以，通常当一项州法律由州官员负责执行时，在法律生效前对他们提起诉讼是很正常的。

sentences.en: So, usually when you have a state law where the state's officials are responsible for enforcing it, it's normal to have a lawsuit filed against them even before it takes effect.
sentences.zh: 但这项法律非常奇怪，而且是故意设计的。

sentences.en: But this law is really strange and intentionally so.
sentences.zh: 所以，无论如何，由于SB8的这个奇怪方面，案件中出现了很多程序上的反复，变得相当复杂。

sentences.en: So, in any event, because of this weird aspect of SB8, there's a lot of procedural back and forth in this case, which gets pretty complicated.
sentences.zh: 但这里重要的是，堕胎服务提供者最终还是告到了最高法院。

sentences.en: But what's important here is that eventually the abortion services providers end up at the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 他们请求发布紧急命令以阻止法律生效。

sentences.en: They ask for an emergency order to stop the law from taking effect.
sentences.zh: 所以换句话说，这并不是通常所谓的“案情实质”诉讼。

sentences.en: So, in other words, it's not a normal so-called merits case.
sentences.zh: 最高法院尚未批准对该案进行全面审查。

sentences.en: The Supreme Court has not granted full review of this case.
sentences.zh: 当然，这意味着没有口头辩论。

sentences.en: Of course, that means there's no oral argument.
sentences.zh: 也没有多轮的简报。

sentences.en: There aren't any multiple rounds of briefing.
sentences.zh: 没有几十份法庭之友陈述书。

sentences.en: There's no dozens of front-of-the-court briefs.
sentences.zh: 对于这一项引发复杂问题的复杂法律，根本没有常规的审查程序。

sentences.en: There's just no regular procedure for reviewing what happens to be a pretty complicated law raising complicated issues.
sentences.zh: 所以，接下来发生的事情正是人们对所谓的“影子案卷”（shadow docket）越来越担心的事情。

sentences.en: So, what happens next is exactly what people are increasingly worried about with the so-called shadow docket.
sentences.zh: 9月1日午夜前夕，最高法院以5比4的投票结果，拒绝在“全女性健康中心诉杰克逊案”中介入。

sentences.en: On September 1st, just before midnight, the Supreme Court, in a 5-4 ruling, refuses to step in, in the case of Whole Woman's Health v.
sentences.zh: 基本上只有一段未署名的文字。

sentences.en: Jackson.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们不是在说该法律是否违宪，但目前程序问题太多，我们不想介入做任何事。

sentences.en: There's basically one unsigned paragraph.
sentences.zh: 还记得我告诉过你程序有时会很令人兴奋吗？

sentences.en: They say, you know, we're not saying whether the law is constitutional or not, but there's just too many procedural issues right now for us to want to step in and do anything.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是一个例子。

sentences.en: Remember how I told you that procedures sometimes can be pretty exciting?
sentences.zh: 所以，这个程序性决定实际上产生了实际影响。

sentences.en: Well, this is an example.
sentences.zh: 最高法院在这里并不是说我们要推翻全国范围内的“罗诉韦德案”，或者在德克萨斯州推翻它（如果这算一回事的话）。

sentences.en: So, this procedural decision actually has a practical effect.
sentences.zh: 但他们的决定意味着在德克萨斯州，堕胎实际上已成为非法。

sentences.en: The Supreme Court isn't saying here that we're overturning Roe v.
sentences.zh: 你无法进行堕胎，因为SB8现在是法律，至少在德克萨斯州是这样。

sentences.en: Wade throughout the country or in Texas, if that were a thing.
sentences.zh: 所以，除非有挑战成功上诉到最高法院，否则这就是德克萨斯州目前的法律。

sentences.en: But the effect of their decision means that in Texas, abortion is pretty much de facto illegal.
sentences.zh: 首席大法官罗伯茨与三位自由派大法官在此案中持异议，我只关注其中一份异议，即索托马约尔大法官的异议，

sentences.en: You can't get an abortion because now SB-8 is the law, at least in Texas.
sentences.zh: 因为她异议的开头值得引用。

sentences.en: So, until and unless there's a challenge that successfully makes its way up to the Supreme Court, that's what the law is in Texas itself.
sentences.zh: 她说，

sentences.en: Chief Justice Roberts, along with the three liberal justices' dissent in this case, and I'll just focus on one of the dissents, Justice Sotomayor's,
sentences.zh: 索托马约尔大法官指出了这项法律的本质。

sentences.en: because the opening of her dissent is worth quoting.
sentences.zh: 她说德克萨斯州立法机构已将该州公民任命为赏金猎人。

sentences.en: She says,
sentences.zh: 她很生气。

sentences.en: And Justice Sotomayor calls the law out for what it is.
sentences.zh: 她以“我持异议”结束了她的异议书。

sentences.en: She says the Texas legislature has deputized the state's citizens as bounty hunters.
sentences.zh: 我特别提到这一点，因为通常大法官们会说“我恭敬地持异议”。

sentences.en: She's mad.
sentences.zh: 这次索托马约尔大法官没有这么说。

sentences.en: She ends her dissent by saying, I dissent.
sentences.zh: 所以，就这样，通过这个所谓的“影子案卷”案件，SB8被允许继续生效。

sentences.en: I note that because normally the justices say, I respectfully dissent.
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么它被称为“影子案卷”案件？

sentences.en: No such thing from Justice Sotomayor this time.
sentences.zh: 大法官们能要求它成为一种实质性案件吗？

sentences.en: So, just like that, with this so-called shadow docket case, SB-8 is allowed to stay in effect.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在这个特定的案件中，由于程序问题，它实际上并没有经过完整的诉讼程序。

sentences.en: And so, why is it a shadow docket case?
sentences.zh: 它处于一种初步阶段。

sentences.en: Like, can the justices require it become a sort of merit case?
sentences.zh: 第五巡回法院只是介入阻止了地方法院暂停该法律的执行。

sentences.en: Well, in this particular case, you know, because of the procedural issues, you know, it hadn't actually been litigated all the way through.
sentences.zh: 所以，

sentences.en: You know, it was at a kind of preliminary stage.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，它实际上并没有完全成熟为最高法院通常会投票决定是否受理的那种案件。

sentences.en: You know, the Fifth Circuit just kind of stepped in to stop the district court from putting a pause on things.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以说，无论如何，这就是他们能做的全部了。

sentences.en: So,
sentences.zh: 但也许思考这个“影子案卷”问题的一种方式是：最高法院在这种情况下应该做什么？

sentences.en: this is a short way of saying it actually didn't sort of fully mature into the kind of case that the Supreme Court usually votes on to decide whether or not they're going to take it or not.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也许当涉及权利且存在潜在的权利侵犯时，他们应该阻止事态恶化。

sentences.en: So, you could say, well, this is kind of all they could do anyway.
sentences.zh: 或者他们根本不应该介入，因为当案件出现在“影子案卷”上时，他们应该在各种案件中保持现状。

sentences.en: But maybe one way of thinking about this shadow docket issue is, well, what is the Supreme Court supposed to do in a situation like this?
sentences.zh: 但问题是法院完全不一致，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, maybe they should stop things from going south when there are rights involved and there are potential infringements of rights.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以说，在这个案件中，他们什么也没做，对吧？

sentences.en: Or they don't get involved ever because they just should keep the status quo in all kinds of cases when they appear on the shadow docket.
sentences.zh: 也许这是一件好事。

sentences.en: But the problem is the court's completely inconsistent, right?
sentences.zh: 他们本不应该在这些“影子案卷”案件中做任何事。

sentences.en: So, you could say that, well, in this case, they didn't do anything, right?
sentences.zh: 但结果证明这取决于主题，因为当涉及到宗教自由权利和新冠疫情限制时，他们非常乐意介入。

sentences.en: And maybe that's a good thing.
sentences.zh: 当涉及到联邦权力的范围以及在大流行期间是否可以实施驱逐禁令时，他们也非常乐意介入。

sentences.en: They're not supposed to do anything in these shadow docket cases.
sentences.zh: 所以，这开始让人们觉得，比起任何一致性，这更多是受主题和五位大法官对此的感受所驱动，而不是因为，嗯，

sentences.en: But it kind of turns out that it depends on the subject matter because when it comes to religious freedom rights and COVID restrictions, they were all too happy to step in.
sentences.zh: 我们不会在有这种紧急程序时介入。

sentences.en: And when it came to the scope of federal power and whether or not you can have an eviction moratorium in a pandemic, they were all too happy to step in.
sentences.zh: 哦，这太严峻了。

sentences.en: So, this starts to strike people as being more motivated by the topic and what five justices feel about it than any consistency in, well,
sentences.zh: 确实很严峻。

sentences.en: we don't step in when we have these kinds of emergency procedures.
sentences.zh: 这太严峻了。

sentences.en: Oh, it's grim.
sentences.zh: 确实很严峻。

sentences.en: It is grim.
sentences.zh: 确实很严峻。

sentences.en: And, in fact, you know,
sentences.zh: 事实上，你知道吗，

sentences.en: one of the things that people are worried about now is that the Supreme Court has already agreed to hear a case in the fall on its normal merits docket that actually is a challenge to a Mississippi law that bans most abortions after 15 weeks of pregnancy.
sentences.zh: 人们现在担心的一件事是，最高法院已经同意在秋季的常规案卷中审理一起案件，这实际上是对密西西比州一项法律的挑战，该法律禁止在怀孕15周后进行大多数堕胎手术。

sentences.en: Of course, that's later than the Texas law.
sentences.zh: 当然，这比德克萨斯州的法律要晚。

sentences.en: The case is called Dobbs, and it's a law that's pretty clearly intended to be a challenge to Roe v.
sentences.zh: 这个案子叫多布斯案（Dobbs），这项法律很明显旨在挑战罗诉韦德案（Roe v. Wade）。

sentences.en: Wade.
sentences.zh: 韦德案。

sentences.en: Now, you might say that, well, in the Texas case, the Supreme Court refused to step in, but they did technically say we're not ruling on the constitutionality of the Texas law.
sentences.zh: 现在，你可能会说，好吧，在德克萨斯州的案件中，最高法院拒绝介入，但他们从技术上讲确实说过我们不对德克萨斯州法律的合宪性做出裁决。

sentences.en: That's technically true, but it's hard not to interpret what they did as bad news for further cutting back on the rights of women when it comes to abortion and the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 这在技术上是正确的，但很难不把他们的做法解读为在堕胎和宪法权利方面进一步削减女性权利的坏消息。

sentences.en: I mean, this tactic of creating a law in which there is no Wade and passing it through with some knuckleheads in state legislature who are not thoughtful about the law at all,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这种创造一种没有“韦德”的法律，并让州议会里一些根本不考虑法律的笨蛋通过它的策略，

sentences.en: is this now a thing?
sentences.zh: 现在成了一种风气吗？

sentences.en: Like, did they just pioneer something horrible that's going to happen in all kinds of states?
sentences.zh: 就像，他们是不是刚刚开创了一种可怕的先例，要在各种州上演？

sentences.en: It seems to be, right?
sentences.zh: 看起来确实如此，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, it does seem to be a novel way of trying to attack a constitutionally established right in a way that's really hard to challenge, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这确实看起来是一种攻击宪法确立的权利的新颖方式，而且很难挑战，对吧？

sentences.en: As you can see from this particular case, right, the one that we just talked about, these abortion services providers had an argument about the constitutionality of SB8,
sentences.zh: 正如你从这个特定的案例中看到的，对吧，就是我们刚才谈到的那个，这些堕胎服务提供者对SB8法案的合宪性提出了质疑，

sentences.en: but it wasn't really clear who they could sue because no one had actually sued them yet, right?
sentences.zh: 但并不清楚他们能起诉谁，因为还没有人真正起诉过他们，对吧？

sentences.en: And it does create an incentive for other states to craft the same kind of version of SB8 for their own states.
sentences.zh: 这确实激励了其他州为自己制定同样版本的SB8法案。

sentences.en: You know, leave it to ordinary private citizens to try and enforce a really restrictive right on abortions.
sentences.zh: 你知道，把执行这种极具限制性的堕胎权的任务留给普通的私人公民。

sentences.en: And it also creates incentives, I think, for states to pass basically vigilante bounty laws for any kind of subject.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，这也激励了各州针对任何议题通过基本上是私刑赏金的法律。

sentences.en: So it doesn't have to be just abortion, right?
sentences.zh: 所以不一定非得是堕胎，对吧？

sentences.en: You could imagine a state thinking, sort of offering a, you know, $10,000 cash prize to allow people to sue others when there's some perceived violation of religious rights,
sentences.zh: 你可以想象一个州会考虑提供，你知道，1万美元的现金奖励，允许人们在认为宗教权利受到侵犯时起诉他人，

sentences.en: free speech rights, you name it.
sentences.zh: 言论自由权，随便什么权利。

sentences.en: But so if we let this go on, there's potentially a snowball effect of, you know, really encouraging this sort of structure to pop up elsewhere throughout the United States.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们任由这种情况继续下去，可能会产生滚雪球效应，你知道，真的会鼓励这种结构在美国各地涌现。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this seems like it's perfectly the purview of the Supreme Court to recognize these as being unconstitutional or constitutional, whatever their decision should be.
sentences.zh: 而且这似乎完全属于最高法院的职权范围，去认定这些是违宪还是合宪，无论他们的决定是什么。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So what is the process for it to sort of,
sentences.zh: 那么，这个过程是怎样的呢，

sentences.en: would it take this case to sort of like make its way up to the Supreme Court for them to be able to make that type of decision or to voice that type of opinion?
sentences.zh: 是否需要这个案件一路打到最高法院，他们才能做出那种决定或发表那种意见？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, that's a good question.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，这是一个好问题。

sentences.en: I think that's less clear.
sentences.zh: 我认为这一点不太清楚。

sentences.en: I mean, I think if there is a case that sort of presents squarely the whether or not Texas's abortion law violates the Constitution,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为如果有一个案件能够直接提出德克萨斯州的堕胎法是否违反宪法的问题，

sentences.en: and it pretty clearly does just on the substance of it, you know, the court's ready to address that.
sentences.zh: 而且仅从实质内容来看，它显然是违宪的，你知道，法院已经准备好处理这个问题了。

sentences.en: I think whether or not the mechanism poses a separate constitutional problem would be something else that a court would have to review as an argument distinct from Roe versus Wade.
sentences.zh: 我认为该机制是否构成了独立的宪法问题，将是法院必须审查的另一个论点，与罗诉韦德案不同。

sentences.en: And whether or not that's a good one is something we've yet to see.
sentences.zh: 至于这是否是一个好的论点，我们还有待观察。

sentences.en: I mean, we didn't see this in the original case that the court reviewed in its shadow docket.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们在法院在影子案卷中审查的最初案件中没有看到这一点。

sentences.en: But it's a good question.
sentences.zh: 但这是一个好问题。

sentences.en: And it's a troubling one, because if we let it go unchecked, right, if we encourage other state legislatures to do the same thing,
sentences.zh: 而且这是一个令人不安的问题，因为如果我们任其发展，对吧，如果我们鼓励其他州议会做同样的事情，

sentences.en: we are incentivizing state legislatures to kind of encourage people to harass others with respect to their constitutional rights.
sentences.zh: 我们就是在激励州议会去鼓励人们骚扰他人的宪法权利。

sentences.en: So in the shadow docket opinion, they mention that it isn't a ruling on the constitutionality of the law itself.
sentences.zh: 所以在影子案卷的意见中，他们提到这并不是对法律本身合宪性的裁决。

sentences.en: When will they rule on the constitutionality of the law itself?
sentences.zh: 他们什么时候会对法律本身的合宪性做出裁决？

sentences.en: They're going to have to wait for that right case, that right opportunity to come up.
sentences.zh: 他们将不得不等待那个合适的案件，那个合适的时机出现。

sentences.en: So right now, because of what the court did on September 1st at midnight, the case just goes back to its process, you know, at the federal district court.
sentences.zh: 所以现在，因为法院在9月1日午夜所做的决定，案件只是回到了联邦地区法院的正常程序中，你知道。

sentences.en: That particular case may go up to the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 那个特定的案件可能会上诉到最高法院。

sentences.en: It may take a different case in Texas that comes up to the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 也可能是一个不同的德克萨斯州案件上诉到最高法院。

sentences.en: And then there's the issue of, in the meantime, the Supreme Court's already decided that they're going to consider an abortion case for its term.
sentences.zh: 而且在此期间还有一个问题，最高法院已经决定在这一任期内审理一起堕胎案件。

sentences.en: That's the Mississippi law.
sentences.zh: 那就是密西西比州的法律。

sentences.en: So a lot of people are just worried anyway that maybe there are already five votes on the court to either radically restrict abortion rights or maybe even do something,
sentences.zh: 所以很多人都很担心，也许法院里已经有五票支持彻底限制堕胎权，甚至可能采取行动，

sentences.en: go as far as overturn Roe versus Wade.
sentences.zh: 走得更远，推翻罗诉韦德案。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And in the meantime, it's illegal to get an abortion in Texas.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在德克萨斯州堕胎是非法的。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, you know, don't forget that just as with Norma McCorvey herself, it's really uneven, right?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，别忘了，就像诺玛·麦考维（Norma McCorvey）本人一样，这非常不公平，对吧？

sentences.en: That when it comes to abortion rights, if you're a person, a wealthy person in Texas, you're going to have access to abortion services providers.
sentences.zh: 当谈到堕胎权时，如果你是一个人，一个德克萨斯州的富人，你就能获得堕胎服务提供者的帮助。

sentences.en: But just like Norma McCorvey herself, who was unemployed at the time her case went up to the court,
sentences.zh: 但就像诺玛·麦考维本人一样，她在案件上诉到法院时失业了，

sentences.en: she was a low-income person who wanted an abortion but really had no easy way to get one.
sentences.zh: 她是一个低收入者，想要堕胎但真的没有简单的方法可以实现。

sentences.en: Abortion rights, frankly, are always about the rights of poor women, right?
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，堕胎权总是关乎贫困女性的权利，对吧？

sentences.en: Who really do not have the means to travel to another state to access an abortion services provider.
sentences.zh: 她们真的没有经济能力去另一个州寻求堕胎服务。

sentences.en: And presumably the person that gave them a right outside of the state could be sued?
sentences.zh: 而且据推测，那个在州外为她们提供权利的人可能会被起诉？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: I told you procedure was interesting.
sentences.zh: 我告诉过你程序问题很有趣。

sentences.en: Procedure is definitely interesting.
sentences.zh: 程序确实很有趣。

sentences.en: Well, thank you so much for this sort of emergency session.
sentences.zh: 好吧，非常感谢你参加这次紧急会议。

sentences.en: I appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我很感激。

sentences.en: Thanks, Roman.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，罗曼。
